## 1. Exact problem and notation

1. Fix an integer `k >= 0` and identify a mask `x < 2^k` with its support
   `supp(x)`, a subset of `[k] = {1,...,k}`.
2. Bitwise OR then becomes set union.
3. For an array `A = (A_1,...,A_n)` of subsets of `[k]`, define
   `U(l,r) = A_l union A_{l+1} union ... union A_r` for `1 <= l <= r <= n`.
4. The goal is to minimize `n` subject to every subset of `[k]`, including the
   empty set, being equal to some `U(l,r)`.
5. Let `N(k)` denote that minimum.
6. Let `nu(k)` denote the corresponding minimum when only the nonempty subsets
   must be represented and every array entry is required to be nonempty.

## 2. Zero separates completely

7. A nonempty interval has union equal to the empty set if and only if every
   entry in that interval is empty.  Hence every full solution contains a zero.
8. Delete every zero from a full solution.  The nonzero entries of any old
   interval become a contiguous interval in the compressed array and have the
   same union.  Thus the compressed array still represents every nonempty set.
9. Conversely, inserting one zero at either end of a nonzero solution represents
   the empty set and preserves every previous interval union.
10. Therefore

       N(k) = nu(k) + 1.

    It is enough to solve the nonzero problem and prepend zero at the end.

## 3. The exact last-occurrence / ordered-partition model

11. Fix a right endpoint `r`.  For each bit `b`, let

       tau_b(r) = max { i <= r : b belongs to A_i },

    with `tau_b(r) = -infinity` if the bit has not appeared.
12. Bit `b` belongs to `U(l,r)` exactly when `tau_b(r) >= l`.
13. Group the currently present bits into blocks having equal last-occurrence
    time, ordered from most recent to least recent:

       P_r = (B_1, B_2, ..., B_t).

14. The distinct suffix unions ending at `r` are exactly

       B_1,
       B_1 union B_2,
       ...,
       B_1 union ... union B_t.

15. In particular, the suffix unions at one endpoint form an inclusion chain
    and there are at most `k` of them in a nonzero construction.
16. If the next array entry is the nonempty set `X`, its bits all acquire the
    new last-occurrence time.  The state transition is exactly

       (B_1,...,B_t)
       -> (X, B_1\X, B_2\X, ..., B_t\X),

    after deleting empty blocks.
17. Thus the problem is equivalently: find the shortest walk through ordered
    set partitions under arbitrary-subset move-to-front operations such that
    every nonempty subset of `[k]` occurs as a prefix union of some visited state.
18. This is the mathematically natural state space.  Searching raw arrays ignores
    the large equivalence induced by identical last-occurrence orders.

## 4. Sperner lower bound

19. Put `m = floor(k/2)` and `M = binom(k,m)`.
20. The `M` subsets of size `m` form a largest antichain in the Boolean lattice.
21. By line 15, one right endpoint can represent at most one member of this
    antichain.
22. Therefore `nu(k) >= M`.

## 5. Why equality in the Sperner bound fails

23. Suppose `k >= 4` and, for contradiction, `nu(k) = M`.
24. Choose one representing interval `I_S` for every `m`-set `S`.
25. If `I_S` contains `I_T`, then `union(I_T) subseteq union(I_S)`.
26. Since `S` and `T` are distinct sets of the same size, no two chosen
    intervals can contain one another.
27. Two chosen intervals cannot share a left endpoint, because then one contains
    the other.  The same holds for right endpoints.
28. There are `M` intervals and only `M` possible endpoints.  Hence their left
    endpoints are all of `1,...,M`, and their right endpoints are also all of
    `1,...,M`.
29. Sort the intervals by left endpoint.  Noncontainment forces their right
    endpoints to be in the same strict order.
30. Consequently the intervals are `[1,1], [2,2], ..., [M,M]`.
31. Every array entry would then itself have size `m >= 2`, making it impossible
    to represent a singleton mask.
32. Hence, for `k >= 4`,

       nu(k) >= M + 1,
       N(k)  >= M + 2.

33. For `k=3`, a separate short argument gives `nu(3) >= 4`: three positions
    must contain the three singleton masks, but a permutation of three distinct
    singletons produces only two of the three two-element sets as adjacent
    unions.

## 6. The interval-slack lemma

34. The same interval argument gives more structure near the lower bound.
35. Let `q` distinct equal-size masks be represented by `q` chosen intervals in
    an array of length `q+d`.
36. The intervals are noncontaining, so their left endpoints and right endpoints
    are separately distinct.
37. After sorting by left endpoint, write the endpoints of interval `i` as

       l_i = i + alpha_i,
       r_i = i + beta_i.

38. Because only `d` of the `q+d` possible endpoints are omitted,
    `0 <= alpha_i,beta_i <= d`.
39. Since `l_i <= r_i`, we have `alpha_i <= beta_i`, and therefore

       length(I_i) = r_i-l_i+1 <= d+1.

40. Applied to a central layer, this says: if `nu(k)=M+d`, every middle-layer
    mask has a representing interval of length at most `d+1`.
41. This converts a global covering problem into a local one whenever `d` is
    small.

## 6a. General rank-count lower bound

41a. Fix any rank `r`, put `m=binom(k,r)`, and suppose the array length is
     `n=m+t`.
41b. For the `m` chosen rank-`r` witnesses, line 37 gives

       I_i subseteq [i,i+t].

41c. Let `J=[a,b]` have length at least `t+1`.  Since `b<=m+t`, necessarily
     `a<=m`; moreover `J` contains `[a,a+t]`, which contains the selected
     rank-`r` witness `I_a`.
41d. Therefore every interval of length at least `t+1` has union of rank at
     least `r`.
41e. Every mask of rank below `r` must consequently be represented by an
     interval of length at most `t`.
41f. The number of such intervals is

       sum_{ell=1}^t (n-ell+1)
       = t*m + binom(t+1,2).

41g. Writing

       L(k,r) = sum_{s=1}^{r-1} binom(k,s),

     every solution must satisfy

       L(k,r) <= t*binom(k,r) + binom(t+1,2).

41h. Define `tau(k,r)` as the least nonnegative integer `t` satisfying that
     inequality.  Equivalently, for `m=binom(k,r)` and `L=L(k,r)`,

       tau(k,r) = ceil((sqrt((2m+1)^2+8L)-(2m+1))/2).

41i. The general nonzero lower bound is therefore

       nu(k) >= B(k) := max_r (binom(k,r)+tau(k,r)).

41j. Its first values are

       B(1),B(2),... = 1,2,4,7,12,21,37,72,128,254,... .

41k. Taking a middle rank and using the central-binomial estimate gives

       nu(k) >= binom(k,floor(k/2))
               + (1+o(1))*sqrt(pi*k/8).

41l. The later containment-multiplicity refinement in paragraphs 663--668
     gives the stronger exact witness-length pruning

       c_s(n)=min( n,
                   min_(r>s) (n-binom(k,r)),
                   min_(r<=s) (n-binom(k,r)+binom(s,r)) ).

     The generic unrestricted generator `exact_or_sat.cpp` now implements
     this simultaneous cap for every rank; source SHA-256 is
     `c1832b235f75be91066fc454ac7c6c46d29610a22aa2826d34c404915600f550`.
     A remote `k=4,n=7` generate/solve/decode regression produced the valid
     word `5,9,1,2,4,8,10`, independently suffix-verified at `15/15` masks.
     The reproduction record is `EXACT_OR_SAT_CONTAINMENT_REGRESSION.md`.
41m. There is a useful refinement of the same count.  Suppose `n=M+d`, where
     `M=binom(k,r)`, and choose one witness for every rank-`r` mask.  If `c` of
     those chosen witnesses have length at most `d`, they share the short
     interval pool with all `L(k,r)` lower masks.  All these physical intervals
     are distinct because their OR values are distinct, so

       L(k,r)+c <= sum_{ell=1}^d (n-ell+1)
                  = d*M+binom(d+1,2).

     Consequently at least

       M - (d*M+binom(d+1,2)-L(k,r))

     chosen rank-`r` witnesses must have the maximum possible length `d+1`
     (when this expression is positive).  For `k=9,n=128,r=5,d=2`, it equals
     all 126 witnesses, proving the forced triple row in line 69m.  For
     `k=10,n=254,r=5,d=2`, it forces at least 130 of the 252 witnesses to be
     triples, but does not force the full `D^2 A` ansatz.  For `n=255,d=3` it
     gives no positive force toward a complete length-four central row.

## 7. Complete classification when d=1

42. Suppose `q` equal-rank masks are represented in `q+1` positions.
43. Let `p` be the omitted left endpoint and `s` the omitted right endpoint.
44. Feasibility of `l_i <= r_i` forces `s <= p`.
45. The sorted representing intervals are exactly

       [i,i]       for i < s,
       [i,i+1]     for s <= i < p,
       [i+1,i+1]   for i >= p.

46. Thus all masks in that antichain are represented by singleton entries or by
    adjacent pairs; the adjacent-pair representatives form one contiguous path
    segment.

## 8. A stronger lower bound for odd k

47. Let `k=2m+1` with `m>=2`.  The ranks `m` and `m+1` both have size
    `M=binom(k,m)`.
48. Assume for contradiction that `nu(k)=M+1`.
49. Apply line 45 to the rank-`m` masks.
50. Every one of the `k` singleton masks must occur literally as an array entry.
51. A singleton entry cannot be one of the singleton-interval representatives
    of an `m`-set because `m>=2`.
52. Therefore the rank-`m` path segment cannot be empty.  In fact, if its two
    omitted endpoints coincided, at most that one uncovered position could be a
    singleton entry, again impossible because there are `k` of them.
53. Hence at least one adjacent pair in the array has union of size exactly `m`.
54. The rank-`m` representative intervals cover every array position when the
    path segment is nonempty.  Consequently every entry has size at most `m`.
55. No entry can therefore itself be an `(m+1)`-set.
56. Apply line 45 to the rank-`m+1` masks.  Since none can be represented by a
    singleton interval, all `M` of them must be represented by the `M` adjacent
    pairs `[1,2],...,[M,M+1]`.
57. Hence every adjacent pair must have union of size `m+1`.
58. This contradicts line 53.
59. Therefore, for odd `k>=5`,

       nu(k) >= M + 2,
       N(k)  >= M + 3.

60. This proves the formerly computational lower bound for `k=5`:
    `nu(5)>=12` and `N(5)>=13`.

## 8a. Equality also fails for even k >= 8

60a. Let `k=2m` and suppose `nu(k)=M+1`, where `M=binom(2m,m)`.
60b. Apply the `d=1` classification in line 45 to all rank-`m` masks.  Outside
     the adjacent-pair path segment, every position is itself a rank-`m` mask.
60c. Inside the path segment, every interval containing at least two positions
     contains one of the selected adjacent pairs, whose union has rank `m`.
60d. Therefore an interval whose union has rank less than `m` must be a singleton
     interval at a position inside the path segment.
60e. Consequently every nonempty mask of rank below `m` must occur literally as
     an array entry.  This requires

       sum_{j=1}^{m-1} binom(2m,j)

     distinct positions.
60f. For `m>=4`, this number is greater than `M+1`; already at `k=8` it is

       binom(8,1)+binom(8,2)+binom(8,3) = 8+28+56 = 92 > 71.

60g. Hence, for every even `k>=8`,

       nu(k) >= M + 2,
       N(k)  >= M + 3.

60h. In particular, `N(8)>=73`; searching nonzero length 71 is mathematically
     pointless.  The first possible nonzero length for `k=8` is 72.

## 10b. Exact k=9 construction and equality-case rigidity

69j. For `k=9`, the rank-count lower bound at rank 5 is attained with
     `m=binom(9,5)=126`, `t=2`, and `n=128`.  There are exactly

       128 + 127 = 255 = sum_{r=1}^4 binom(9,r)

     intervals of lengths one and two and exactly 255 masks below rank 5.
69k. The proof of the rank-count bound therefore forces equality everywhere:
     the 128 entries and 127 adjacent-pair unions are 255 distinct masks and
     enumerate every mask of ranks 1 through 4 exactly once.
69l. Put `P_i=A_i union A_{i+1}`.  Adjacent entries must be incomparable;
     otherwise `P_i` would duplicate one of its endpoint entries.  Hence no
     entry can have rank 4, because its union with either incomparable neighbor
     would have rank at least 5.  It follows that:

       * the entries have ranks at most 3;
       * 126 of the 127 masks `P_i` are all rank-4 masks;
       * the remaining exceptional `P_i` has rank 2 or 3.

69m. The interval-slack lemma makes every rank-5 witness have length at most
     three.  Lengths one and two are already occupied by lower masks, so the
     126 length-three windows are exactly all 126 rank-5 masks.  Equivalently,

       Q_i = P_i union P_{i+1}

     enumerates the complete rank-5 layer.
69n. Thus an optimal central skeleton is an alternating Hamilton path through
     all rank-4 and rank-5 masks in the middle-levels incidence graph, with one
     exceptional rank-2 or rank-3 `P` vertex.  The successful search also used
     the dual graded conditions that every rank-3 mask occurs as an adjacent
     `P` intersection and every rank-6 mask occurs as an adjacent `Q` union.

## 11. Current general upper bounds

70. Known one-bit covering words give valid nonzero lengths 40, 76, and 149 for
    `k=7,8,9`; arbitrary masks improve these values to 37, 72, and 128.
71. Starting with any nonzero construction `B=(b_1,...,b_n)` on `k` bits, put
    `h=2^k` and form the trimmed lift

       B' = B || [h] || [h OR b_1, ..., h OR b_{n-1}].

72. The first copy covers all old nonzero masks and `[h]` covers the new
    singleton.  To cover `h OR s`, choose an old witness `b_i,...,b_j` for `s`.
    If `j<n`, use its transformed copy.  If `j=n`, use the first-copy suffix
    `b_i,...,b_n` followed by `[h]`.  Both intervals have union `h OR s`.
73. Hence the stronger recurrence

       nu(k+1) <= 2 nu(k)

    holds.  The previously used `2 nu(k)+1` lift had one redundant final entry.
73a. Lifting the exact length-254 `k=10` construction gives nonzero length
     `254*2^(k-10)` and full length `254*2^(k-10)+1` for every `k>=10`.
74. The older one-bit length-149 base and lifts from `k=8,9` are superseded by
    the exact `k=10` base.
75. These are verified upper bounds only; they are not claims of optimality.

       lower   1  2  3  5  8 13 22 38  73  129  255  466  927 1720

## 13. Promising combinatorial reformulations

81. For even `k=2m`, attaining `nu(k)=M+1` forces every middle `m`-set to be an
    array entry or an adjacent union, by line 45.
82. In the extreme path case, define

       T_i = A_i union A_{i+1},  i=1,...,M.

    Then `(T_1,...,T_M)` is a permutation of all `m`-subsets.
83. An internal array entry satisfies

       A_i subseteq T_{i-1} intersection T_i,

    while the two neighboring entries together must cover each `T_i`.
84. If consecutive `T_i` are adjacent in the Johnson graph `J(k,m)`, their
    intersection has size `m-1`.  This suggests searching Hamilton paths in the
    Johnson graph together with compatible endpoint labels `A_i`, rather than
    searching arbitrary arrays.
85. The literature on cyclic sequences of subsets with distinct consecutive
    unions is directly relevant to this middle-layer skeleton, but distinct
    consecutive unions alone do not guarantee coverage of the other ranks.
86. For odd `k=2m+1`, both central ranks must be handled simultaneously.  This
    coupling is exactly what proves line 59 and is likely the source of further
    lower bounds.

## 13a. The OR-derivative triangle and exact central-row factorization

86a. For a set sequence `X=(X_1,...,X_s)`, define its union derivative by

       (D X)_i = X_i union X_{i+1}.

     Associativity and idempotence of union give

       (D^q X)_i = X_i union X_{i+1} union ... union X_{i+q}.

     Thus every interval union of `A` is an entry of exactly one row in the
     triangle `A, D A, D^2 A, ...`.  This is an OR analogue of Pascal's
     triangle and is the cleanest language for fixed-window constructions.

86b. Fix a proposed central row `T=(T_1,...,T_M)` and `d>=0`.  There exists
     `A=(A_1,...,A_{M+d})` with

       T = D^d A

     if and only if, for each bit separately, every run of 1s strictly inside
     its length-`M` incidence word in `T` has length at least `d+1`.  A run
     touching the left or right boundary may be shorter.

86c. Proof of necessity: one occurrence of a bit in `A_j` turns on precisely
     the central-window starts

       [j-d,j] intersect [1,M].

     This is an internal block of `d+1` ones, truncated only at a boundary.
     The support of that bit in `T` is a union of such blocks.

86d. Proof of sufficiency: an internal run `[p,q]` of length at least `d+1`
     is the union of the blocks generated by positions `p+d,...,q` in `A`.
     A boundary run is generated by the corresponding truncated block(s).
     Do this independently for every bit.

86e. The coordinatewise largest factor is particularly simple:

       A_j^max = intersection of T_i over
                 max(1,j-d) <= i <= min(M,j).

     Every factor has `A_j subseteq A_j^max`; under the run condition, the
     maximal factor itself satisfies `D^d A^max=T`.

86f. The central row controls both sides, but by dual operations.  Above it,

       D^(d+q) A = D^q T,

     so coverage is controlled by consecutive unions in `T`.  Below it, for
     `0<=q<d`,

       (D^q A)_i subseteq
       intersection of T_j over
       max(1,i+q-d) <= j <= min(i,M).

     Hence lower-rank flexibility comes from consecutive intersections in
     `T`.  A Hamilton path in a Johnson graph is only the middle skeleton; it
     must have rich union shadows above and intersection shadows below.

86f1. There is a useful sharpening for the maximal factor.  Coordinatewise
      erosion followed by a shorter dilation shows, under the run condition,

       (D^q A^max)_i =
       intersection of T_j over
       max(1,i+q-d) <= j <= min(i,M),       0<=q<=d.

      If consecutive `T_i` are Johnson-adjacent rank-`r` sets and `d<=r`, the
      removed bits in any `d` consecutive transitions are distinct: repeating
      one would create an internal 1-run of length at most `d`.  Therefore all
      internal entries in row `q` of the maximal lower triangle have rank

       r-d+q.

      For `k=10,n=255`, this predicts the natural strict grading

       ranks 1,2 in A; rank 3 in D A; rank 4 in D^2 A;
       rank 5 in D^3 A.

      For `n=254`, it predicts ranks 1,2,3 in `A`, rank 4 in `D A`, and
      rank 5 in `D^2 A`.  Boundary envelopes can be larger, but their labels
      may be reduced to submasks.  `graded_array_sat.cpp` uses this as a
      sufficient search restriction in the `k=10` models.

86g. Important logical boundary: if `n=M+d`, universality alone does *not*
     force the `M` windows of length `d+1` to enumerate a chosen rank layer;
     its rank witnesses may have varying shorter lengths.  Requiring
     `D^d A` to be a permutation of that layer is a strong sufficient
     construction ansatz, not a general characterization of every optimum.
     Under that ansatz, however, the factorization lemma is exact.

86h. This leads to a precise sufficient recipe for attaining `B(k)`.  Choose
     a maximizing rank `r`, let `M=binom(k,r)` and `d=B(k)-M`, order all
     rank-`r` sets as `T`, require the run condition, factor `T=D^d A`, and
     arrange that the union derivatives of `T` cover all upper ranks while
     the lower rows of `A` cover all lower ranks.  Such an `A` has length
     `B(k)` and is automatically optimal.  The conjecture

       nu(k) = B(k)

     is verified for `k<=10`, but remains unproved from `k=11` onward.

86i. The exact `k=9` skeleton gives an explicit Hamilton path through the
     complete rank-5 layer on ten bits.  Write its 127 adjacent-pair values as
     `P_i` (all 126 four-sets plus one exception) and its 126 triple values as
     `Q_i=P_i union P_{i+1}` (all five-sets).  With new bit `h=2^9`, interleave

       h union P_1, Q_1, h union P_2, Q_2, ...,
       Q_126, h union P_127

     and delete the unique lifted exceptional `P`.  The remaining 252 terms
     are exactly all ten-bit five-sets.  Consecutive terms are Johnson-adjacent;
     across the deletion this follows from the rank-6 union of consecutive
     `Q` values.  This path is stored in `k10_middle_path_seed.txt`.
     It is not itself factorable at slack 2 or 3 because the new bit alternates,
     creating internal runs of length one.  It is a useful exact seed and a
     warning that Hamiltonicity and shadow coverage do not imply factorability.

## 13b. Complement-symmetric middle paths for even k

86j. When `k=2r`, complementation is an automorphism of the middle-layer
     Johnson graph `J(2r,r)`.  Pair every rank-`r` set `X` with its complement
     `X^c`.  There are `binom(2r,r)/2` such antipodal pairs.

86k. Let `P=(P_1,...,P_{M/2})` contain one representative of every antipodal
     pair and suppose

       P_i is Johnson-adjacent to P_{i+1},
       P_{M/2} is Johnson-adjacent to P_1^c.

     Then

       T = P_1,...,P_{M/2}, P_1^c,...,P_{M/2}^c

     is a Hamilton cycle in `J(2r,r)` (written with one cyclic edge cut).  The
     second half repeats the first half's exchange pattern under complement.

86l. This is equivalently a Hamilton cycle in the quotient by complementation
     with odd voltage.  Choose a canonical representative `R_v` for every
     antipodal pair.  A quotient edge `uv` has parity 0 when `R_u` is adjacent
     to `R_v`, and parity 1 when `R_u` is adjacent to `R_v^c`.  An ordering of
     all quotient vertices lifts to the displayed antipodal Hamilton cycle
     exactly when the xor of its edge parities is 1.  This reduces the ten-bit
     middle-layer search from 252 vertices to 126 without losing any five-set.

86m. Complementation exchanges intersections and unions:

       (X_1 intersection ... intersection X_q)^c
         = X_1^c union ... union X_q^c.

     Therefore the intersection shadows of the first half are mirrored by
     union shadows in the second half, and conversely.  With the cyclic seam
     treated consistently, a missing rank-`r-j` shadow is paired with a
     missing rank-`r+j` shadow.  This turns the formerly separate lower-shadow
     and upper-shadow objectives into one self-dual objective.

86n. This symmetry does not by itself solve the construction: the incidence
     runs must still satisfy the factorization condition, and the resulting
     factor must still be labeled to cover ranks below the central lower
     shadow.  It is nevertheless a genuine reduction.  The experimental
     implementation is `antipodal_central_search.cpp`.  The eventual exact
     ten-bit path was found in the unrestricted factorable component rather
     than the antipodal subfamily, using `central_path_plateau.cpp`.

## 14. Concrete instructions for the next mathematical attack

87. The next unresolved target is `k=11`.  The proved nonzero lower bound is
    `B(11)=465`, while the certified partial-factor completion in Section 161
    gives `nu(11)<=477`; equivalently,

       466 <= N(11) <= 478.

87a. The ten-bit success gives a reproducible search pattern for the next
     attack: construct a factorable central Johnson path, optimize its complete
     two-sided shadows by deterministic neutral moves, then solve only the
     lower factor labels exactly.  The crucial ten-bit transition was

       966/968 shadows -> 967/968 -> 968/968

     within seven factor-preserving 2-opt moves.  This avoided a monolithic
     SAT search over all array bits.
87b. For `k=11`, the maximizing layer has `M=binom(11,6)=462` and slack 3 at
     the lower bound.  The corresponding sharp central ansatz is therefore

       T=D^3 A,

     with 462 rank-6 sets and a factor of length 465.  As before, this is a
     sufficient construction ansatz, not a theorem that every optimum must
     have this form.
88. Score candidates by all prefix unions of the recency partitions, with extra
    weight on the rare ranks 1, 2, `k-2`, and `k-1`; middle-rank coverage is built
    into the structural search and should not dominate the objective.
89. Every claimed construction must be checked independently by the `O(nk)`
    suffix-OR recurrence.  Every claimed lower bound must be a proof or an
    auditable UNSAT certificate, not failure of a heuristic search.

## 15. Useful references and warning

90. The stricter one-bit problem is OEIS A348574:
    <https://oeis.org/A348574>.
91. A relevant consecutive-union paper is Mueller--Jimbo, *Cyclic sequences of
    k-subsets with distinct consecutive unions*:
    <https://www.audiolabs-erlangen.de/content/05_fau/professor/00_mueller/03_publications/2008_MuellerJimbo_CyclicSequences_DM.pdf>.
92. Do not confuse a construction for the one-bit variant, a middle-layer
    enumeration, or the doubling lift with a shortest construction for the
    unrestricted problem.
93. The current frontier is exact through `k=10` and also at `k=12`; the first
    unresolved case is `k=11`, with `466 <= N(11) <= 478`.
94. The quotient-and-lift language in Section 13b is standard Hamilton
    compression terminology; see Gregor--Merino--Muetze, *The Hamilton
    compression of highly symmetric graphs*:
    <https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.08126>.  The two-sided OR-shadow requirement
    imposed here is additional and is not supplied by that paper.

## 16. General asymptotic constructions supplied after the exact k=10 result

95. Keep the zero convention explicit.  Let `nu(k)` denote the optimum for
    the `2^k-1` nonzero masks.  For the original problem, which also asks for
    mask zero and uses nonempty intervals,

       N(k) = nu(k) + 1.

    A literal zero is necessary for mask zero.  Zero entries can be deleted
    only when discussing the nonzero-only problem.

96. A simple Cartesian symmetric-chain construction proves, for every split
    `k=a+b`,

       nu(k) <= W(b)(2^a-1) + W(a)(2^b-1),
       W(t)=binom(t,floor(t/2)).

    For each chain `C`, reverse its nonzero increment word on the left and use
    the forward increment word on the right.  Their boundary realizes the
    complete Cartesian product of the two chains.  This has asymptotic ratio
    `2 sqrt(2)` to `W(k)`.

97. A stronger complement-bridge Euler construction uses only the top-level
    long chains on one side.  For `k=p+q`, it has exact length

       C_q (2^(p-1)+2 C_(p-1)-2)
       + C_(p-1) (2^q+C_q-2) + (q mod 2),

    where `C_t=W(t)`.  Its proof uses a bidirected complete bipartite Euler
    tour and the fact that, for every `X` in the `p`-cube, either the SCD chain
    of `X` or the SCD chain of its complement is a top-level long chain.  A
    balanced split gives `(sqrt(2)+o(1))W(k)`.

98. An antipodal-chain rectangle schedule gives the same leading constant and
    permits endpoint fusions.  For even `s,t`, with `p=W(s), q=W(t)`, the
    claimed explicit nonzero length is

       2^(s-1) q + 2^(t-1) p
       + min(pq-p-q, p+q-2) + Delta(s,t),

       Delta(s,t)=min(floor((2^s+p-2)/p),
                      floor((2^t+q-2)/q)).

    The connector and simultaneous-fusion arguments are combinatorially
    consistent.  This yields the proved asymptotic bracket

       (1+o(1)) W(k) <= nu(k) <= (sqrt(2)+o(1)) W(k).

99. These asymptotic families do not improve the current finite `k<20`
    constructor.  The stored finite bases are now the exact solutions through
    ten, the completed length-477 word at eleven, the exact length-926 word at
    twelve, and the cross-seam-completed length-3676 word at fourteen.  The trimmed lift

       nu(k+1) <= 2 nu(k)

    propagates the fourteen-bit base to nonzero lengths
    `7352,14704,29408,58816,117632` for `k=15,...,19`.  Exact central search
    remains the relevant route for closing the gaps.

## 17. Sharpened k=11 middle-level formulation

100. A rank-6 Johnson path with 461 distinct adjacent intersections is an
     alternating Hamilton path through all 462 rank-6 vertices and 461 of the
     462 rank-5 vertices.  It closes to a middle-levels Hamilton cycle through
     the omitted rank-5 vertex only when that omitted mask is contained in
     **both** rank-6 endpoints; distinct intersections alone do not imply this
     endpoint condition.  At an internal rank-5 vertex `C`, choosing the two incident path
     edges to `C+x` and `C+y` makes the corresponding adjacent rank-6 union
     exactly `C+{x,y}`.  Thus complete rank-7 shadow is a local SAT condition
     on pairs of selected middle-level edges.

101. Three consecutive rank-6 vertices form a selected alternating path of
     four middle-level edges.  Requiring such a path for each rank-8 union and
     for each rank-4 intersection gives local SAT encodings of the second
     upper and lower shadows.  The implementation is `middle_levels_sat.cpp`.

102. Fixing the deleted rank-5 vertex is WLOG by bit symmetry.  Short cyclic
     coordinate runs of lengths two or three are forbidden unless they cross
     this distinguished cut.  Coverage witnesses using the cut are excluded.
     Consequently, any satisfying Hamilton cycle yields after cutting:

       * a factorable rank-6 path `T=D^3 A`;
       * 461 distinct internal rank-5 intersections, with the omitted one
         available at both endpoints;
       * complete rank-4, rank-7, and rank-8 shadows.

     The remaining checks are rank 3, ranks 9--11, and exact lower pin labels.
     This is a compact structural SAT search, not the full 11-by-465 bit model.

## 18. Unrestricted near-width normal form

103. For an array of length `n=M+d`, choose one witness interval for every
     rank-`r` mask and order them by left endpoint.  Equal-rank masks are
     incomparable, so the right endpoints increase in the same order.  Hence

       I_i=[i+alpha_i,i+beta_i],
       0<=alpha_1<=...<=alpha_M<=d,
       0<=beta_1<=...<=beta_M<=d,
       alpha_i<=beta_i.

     The pair `(alpha_i,beta_i)` changes at most `2d` times.  Thus the fully
     unrestricted central witnesses form at most `2d+1` fixed-window regimes,
     rather than an arbitrary interval family.  This is the correct extension
     of the fixed-row ansatz when that ansatz is not forced.

104. Prescribed interval unions have an exact coordinatewise factorization
     criterion.  Given targets `T_i` on intervals `I_i`, define for every bit
     `x`

       Z_x = [n] minus union_{i: x notin T_i} I_i.

     A factor exists iff `I_i intersect Z_x` is nonempty for every `x in T_i`.
     Every factor is obtained by independently choosing a hitting set
     `H_x subset Z_x` for the positive intervals and putting `x` in `A_j`
     exactly when `j in H_x`.  A separate condition is needed if every array
     entry is required to be nonzero.

105. Let `L=sum_{s<r} binom(k,s)` (excluding rank zero) and let

       sigma = d M + binom(d+1,2) - L.

     At most `sigma` rank-`r` masks can use witnesses of length at most `d`.
     Therefore at least `M-sigma` of the `M` length-`d+1` windows are distinct
     rank-`r` masks.  When `sigma=0`, the fixed central row and the collision-
     free lower triangle are forced, making the derivative/pinning formulation
     necessary and sufficient.  For `k=11,r=6,d=3`, however, `sigma=369`, so
     the current fixed-row search remains a sufficient ansatz rather than a
     proof about all potential length-465 optima.

## 20. Odd-to-even central concatenation

114. There is a useful near-exact lift from a middle-level path in odd
     dimension.  Let `k=2r-1`, let `T=(T_0,...,T_{M-1})` enumerate all
     rank-`r` sets, and suppose its adjacent intersections

        C_i=T_i intersect T_(i+1)

     are distinct.  They then comprise all but one of the `M` rank-`(r-1)`
     sets; call the omitted set `C*`.  Orient `T` so that `C*` is contained in
     `T_(M-1)`.  On adding a new coordinate `z`, the concatenation

        P = T_0,...,T_(M-1),
            z+C*, z+C_(M-2), z+C_(M-3), ..., z+C_0

     is a Hamilton path through all rank-`r` sets of the `(k+1)`-cube.  The
     boundary is valid because `C* subset T_(M-1)`; consecutive `C_i` are
     distinct rank-`(r-1)` subsets of `T_(i+1)` and therefore differ by one
     exchange.  The implementation is `odd_to_even_central.cpp`.

115. This concatenation preserves all lower intersection shadows: windows in
     the first half give the masks without `z`; windows in the second half are
     `z` plus the corresponding one-order-deeper intersections of `T`; and the
     cross-boundary intersection supplies `C*`.  On the upper side,
     consecutive unions inside the `C` half recover every `T_i` except the
     opposite endpoint, so exactly the mask `z+T_0` is absent from the first
     upper layer.  Longer `C`-windows recover the corresponding shorter
     `T`-windows except for an endpoint window at each length; those endpoint
     values may occur elsewhere, but this needs to be checked rather than
     assumed.  Hence the lift loses at most a small endpoint family of upper
     values, not a positive fraction of a layer.  On the exact `k=9` path it
     produces a
     252-vertex rank-5 path for `k=10` with complete ranks 3--5 and 7--10 and
     exactly one missing rank-6 mask.

116. The coordinate-run condition transforms favorably when the required
     factor slack drops by one.  An internal run of length at least `d+1` in
     `T` induces an internal run of length at least `d` in its adjacent-
     intersection path.  Thus a factorable odd path with slack `d` gives a
     factorable even concatenation when the even problem has slack `d-1`.
     In particular, the desired `k=11,d=3` path would yield a factorable
     `k=12,d=2` central path with only a small endpoint family of missing upper
     masks (and necessarily one in rank 7).  The older
     `k=9,d=2` to `k=10,d=2` experiment has run deficit 41, exactly because
     there is no slack drop there.

117. Applying the lower-preserving lift to `k11_lower956_upper549.txt` already
     gives the 924-vertex path `k12_lift_from_k11_upper549.txt`.  Its rank-4
     and rank-5 lower shadows are complete.  It misses 28 upper masks and has
     exactly one unit of run deficit, caused by the unavoidable two-term run

## 21. Stronger exact connectivity encoding for the k=11 search

122. `recombine_paths_sat.cpp` now has an `ord` family of modes that eliminates
     disconnected cycle covers in the initial SAT model rather than adding
     connectivity cuts afterward.  Give every selected undirected edge exactly
     one direction, require one selected incoming and one selected outgoing arc
     at every real vertex and at the dummy vertex, and attach a nine-bit
     position to each of the 462 real vertices.  An arc from the dummy fixes its
     head at position 1; every selected real arc `u->v` enforces

        position(v) = position(u)+1 mod 512.

     A directed component not containing the dummy would be a real cycle of
     length `L<=462` and would imply `position=position+L mod 512`, impossible
     because `0<L<512`.  Hence every model is one Hamilton cycle through the
     dummy, equivalently a Hamilton path on the real rank-6 vertices.  This
     binary-order proof is exact and uses only nine position bits per vertex.
     A sanity instance with the rank-7 and rainbow-edge conditions returned a
     single 463-vertex cycle at the first SAT call.

123. The full-graph model also uses exact WLOG symmetry breaking.  The 461
     distinct rank-5 edge colours omit exactly one of the 462 rank-5 sets.  A
     bit permutation sends it to `31={0,1,2,3,4}`.  Its stabilizer sends an
     endpoint containing it to `63`, path reversal makes `63` the first
     vertex, and the remaining stabilizer sends its first neighbor to `119`.
     Thus the canonical path begins `63,119`, and colour 31 is forbidden while
     every other rank-5 colour is explicitly required.  The score-549 seed,
     when reversed, already has this canonical prefix, so the symmetry clauses
     preserve its complete phase assignment.

124. The current `hybrid` exact mode requires all rank-7 edge unions, all
     rank-4 triple intersections, all rank-8 triple unions, the omitted-colour
     endpoint condition, Hamilton connectivity, and the run constraints up
     front.  It adds rank-3 and rank-9 path witnesses only if a connected model
     actually misses them.  Pair/path witness variables are now defined in
     both directions, not merely by witness-to-edge implications, which gives
     substantially stronger unit propagation.  Full Johnson degree-at-most-two
     constraints use sequential counters rather than roughly two million
     triple clauses.  Exact searches are running both without a distance
     restriction and with at most 24 or 36 dropped edges from the score-549
     path.  Separately, rank-7-complete ordered base models are being generated
     as a diverse edge portfolio; a ten-path sparse hybrid union was proved
     UNSAT, while larger unions remain under test.

## 22. Necessary unrestricted middle-layer forest

125. A useful takeover report supplied after the fixed-row work proves a
     genuinely unrestricted theorem.  Let `k=2p+1`,
     `M=binom(k,p)=binom(k,p+1)`, and choose one witness interval for every
     rank-`p` and rank-`(p+1)` mask in an array of length `M+d`.  Join a lower
     and upper mask by an `L` edge when their witnesses share a left endpoint,
     and by an `R` edge when they share a right endpoint.  Each edge is an
     inclusion `C subset T`; each color is a matching; and no pair has both
     colors.  Orient `L` from lower to upper and `R` from upper to lower.  Along
     an `L` edge the right endpoint strictly increases, and along an `R` edge
     the left endpoint strictly increases.  An alternating cycle is therefore
     impossible.  The union is a spanning linear forest.

126. Each rank uses `M` distinct left endpoints and `M` distinct right
     endpoints among `M+d` positions, so each color has at least `M-d` edges.
     If the forest has `c` components, then

        c = (M-|L|)+(M-|R|) <= 2d.

     On either layer the degree deficit from two is `c`, hence at least `M-c`
     masks have degree two.  For `k=11,n=465`, this forces at most six
     components, at least 459 edges of each color, and at least 456 two-sided
     flags in each of ranks 5 and 6.  This is the correct necessary
     unrestricted replacement for treating the fixed row `D^3 A` as a normal
     form; the fixed-row path is only a special sufficient case.

127. The same endpoint counting gives a forced adjacent-shadow theorem.  For
     selected ranks `s` and `s+1` in length `n`, all but at most
     `2(n-binom(k,s+1))` rank-`s` masks are intersections of two selected
     rank-`(s+1)` masks, with the dual union statement above.  At `k=11,n=465`
     this forces at least 324/330 rank-4 intersections and 324/330 rank-7
     unions.  Intersections of endpoint sets also force at least 24 common
     rank-3/4/5/6 flags of physical lengths exactly 1,2,3,4, and interval-pool
     counting forces at least 93 rank-6 witnesses of length four, at least 87
     of them internal forest vertices.  These constraints are promising for a
     future six-component unrestricted SAT formulation; they do not themselves
     construct or rule out a 465-entry array.

## 23. Audited dimension reductions from the exact k=12 optimum

128. Every join-homomorphism of Boolean cubes preserves interval-OR
     universality: if `phi(x OR y)=phi(x) OR phi(y)`, applying `phi` entrywise
     maps a witness of `S` to a witness of `phi(S)`.  All 12 coordinate erasures
     and all `binom(12,2)=66` coordinate identifications were applied to the
     exact 926-entry `k=12` array and then greedily pruned in many orders.  The
     best entrywise quotient has length 627.  A stronger literal filter deletes
     every entry carrying one chosen coordinate before compressing the other
     coordinates; this is valid because a witness for a target excluding that
     coordinate cannot contain a contaminated entry.  The twelve filtered
     lengths are

        671,668,675,670,673,674,672,666,661,669,664,641,

     and randomized deletion pruning reaches 583.  Neither method improves the
     existing k=11 upper bound 508.

129. Filtering the rank-6 central path itself is structurally more informative.
     For each deleted coordinate it leaves exactly all `binom(11,6)=462`
     rank-6 masks.  The best coordinate is the twelfth: all upper shadows are
     complete, but the induced order has 24 non-Johnson jumps, 104 forbidden
     internal coordinate runs with total factorization deficit 163, and lower
     shadow omissions `3,21,34` in ranks 3,4,5.  Thus the exact k=12 path gives
     a strong k=11 upper-shadow seed, not a reverse exact lift.

## 24. First structured k=13 and k=14 attacks

130. A one-interface k=13 construction (all entries excluding the new bit
     followed by all entries containing it) has a sharp internal obstruction.
     Its no-new-bit prefix must itself be universal on 12 bits, hence has length
     at least 926.  The 924 masks `{h} union S`, `|S|=6`, form an antichain, and
     suffix ORs ending at one fixed position form a chain; consequently the
     new-bit suffix needs at least 924 endpoints.  Every one-interface
     construction therefore has length at least 1850.  In particular the
     tempting lower-bound-length split `926+1+792=1719` is impossible: only 792
     transformed endpoints are available for those 924 central masks.  An
     exact sweep of all two deletions from both orientations of the standard
     lift found no length-1851 construction; the best covers 4094/4096 old
     masks, missing `1616` and `1876` after removal of the high bit.  Exhaustive
     one- and two-entry submask repairs do not close this two-mask gap.  Exact
     multi-position repairs remain under test.

131. The more promising even target is k=14.  With two new bits, the middle
     layer splits as

        binom(12,7)+2 binom(12,6)+binom(12,5)
        = 792+924+924+792 = binom(14,7)=3432.

     The four types `00,01,10,11` therefore align with the rank-7, rank-6,
     rank-6, rank-5 layers of the solved 12-cube.  A square-lift Johnson path
     was built by joining reflected rank-7/rank-5 cycles to forward and reverse
     copies of the exact k=12 central path.  It is a valid Hamilton path.  Both
     k=13 and k=14 central searches quickly reached factorization deficit zero,
     so the live obstruction is simultaneous lower/upper shadow coverage, not
     the coordinate-run condition.  At the current checkpoint the targeted
     k=13 upper phase misses 87 rank-8, 12 rank-9, and one rank-10 mask; the
     targeted k=14 lower phase continues to improve ranks 5 and 6.  These are
     search checkpoints, not universal arrays or improved rigorous upper
     bounds.

## 25. Audit of the rainbow-overlap and Pascal-splicing proposals

132. The later complement-bridge note does not improve the finite-dimensional
     bounds in this project.  Its construction and exact length are the same
     proved complement-bridge Euler family already recorded in paragraph 97.
     Minimizing its formula gives nonzero lengths `3361` and `6740` for
     `k=13,14`, whereas the exact `k=12` lift gives `1852` and `3704`.
     Its role is therefore asymptotic: it proves

        nu(k) <= (sqrt(2)+o(1)) W(k),

     but it supplies neither an exact `k<20` certificate nor a new lower
     bound.

133. The proposed rainbow OR-overlap graph is an exact reformulation of the
     fixed-window ansatz, not a reduction of it.  For delay `d`, take vertices
     to be ordered `d`-tuples of factor labels and edges to be ordered
     `(d+1)`-tuples, colored by their OR.  A trail using every rank-`r` color
     once is exactly a factor word whose length-`d+1` windows enumerate the
     rank-`r` layer.  This automatically combines central ordering and
     factorization, but the unrestricted colored graph is enormous: even one
     rank-`r` color has up to `(2^(d+1)-1)^r` coordinatewise pin patterns.
     The existing central-path plus coordinatewise pinning formulation is the
     compressed representation of the same freedom.

134. The suggested sparse subgraph in which the `d+1` labels of every colored
     edge are pairwise disjoint imposes a much stronger, previously unstated
     condition.  Let `h=d+1`, and consider one coordinate with an internal run
     `[p,q]` in the central incidence word.  If `H` is the set of factor
     positions carrying that coordinate, pairwise disjointness in every
     `h`-window forces consecutive pins to be at distance at least `h`.
     Continuous coverage of the central run forces their distance to be at
     most `h`.  Since the run is internal, its first and last pins are forced
     to positions `p+d` and `q`.  Hence all pin gaps equal `h` and

        q-p+1 is divisible by h.

     Ordinary factorability requires only `q-p+1 >= h`.  Thus the disjoint
     rainbow subgraph discards most factorable central paths; it should be
     treated as a special experimental ansatz, not as the general route.

135. Pascal splicing is sound only conditionally.  If two factor words have
     identical length-`d` endpoint signatures, overlapping those signatures
     factors the concatenated central rows.  What remains unproved is exactly
     the hard part: the two recursively constructed rows must admit compatible
     signatures, the new coordinate must be pinned without contaminating the
     old block, and all seam-crossing lower and upper shadows must be repaired.
     The statement that defects are localized at the seam is useful for
     heuristic seed construction, but there is no bounded-seam repair theorem.
     The current `k=14` square lift is already a more concrete instance of this
     recursive philosophy.

136. Two exact central skeletons now sharpen the `k=13` search.  First, a SAT
     construction gives a Hamilton ordering of all 1716 rank-7 masks whose
     adjacent unions cover all 1287 rank-8 masks; its factorization deficit is
     351 before run repair.  Second, Knuth's star-transposition middle-levels
     cycle gives a deterministic rank-7 ordering whose 1715 adjacent rank-6
     intersections are all distinct, with the omitted rank-6 mask available
     at the cut; its initial factorization deficit is 919.  Exact lazy-run SAT
     searches are repairing these upper-complete and lower-rainbow skeletons.
     They are materially stronger seeds, but neither is yet a length-1719
     universal array.

## 26. Audit of the wide-shadow erosion proposal

137. The erosion transformation is a correct conditional theorem.  Let a
     cyclic row `T` have no coordinate 1-run shorter than `h+1`, and set

        E_i = intersection(T_(i-h),...,T_i).

     Then, for `0 <= q <= h`, coordinatewise interval geometry gives

        OR(E_i,...,E_(i+q))
          = intersection(T_(i+q-h),...,T_i).

     Indeed, if the shorter interval on the right lies in a coordinate run,
     the unused left and right margins of that run have total length at least
     `q`; consequently one of the `q+1` length-`h+1` erosion windows lies
     wholly inside the run.  The converse containment is immediate.  It
     follows that a cyclic middle row with complete intersection and union
     shadows through depth `h` yields a universal nonzero array of length at
     most

        L + 2h + 2 sum_(s=0)^(k/2-h-1) binom(k,s) - 1

     in even dimension (with the tail count interpreted as zero when the
     central band is the whole lattice).  Zero erosion entries, if any, can be
     deleted without harming nonzero coverage.

138. Taking `h > (1/2+o(1)) sqrt(k log k)` makes the literal binomial tails
     `o(W(k))`.  Therefore the proposed wide-shadow-row lemma with
     `L=(1+o(1))W(k)` would genuinely prove

        nu(k) = (1+o(1)) W(k).

     This is a clean equivalence target, but the lemma itself is wholly
     unproved.  The construction chooses the coordinatewise maximal factor of
     the central row.  It removes the later pin-label SAT problem only by
     demanding that this particular maximal factor already have every lower
     shadow.  That is substantially stronger than ordinary factorability and
     is not implied by known Johnson-graph Hamiltonicity.

139. The four-block Pascal braid correctly enumerates the child layer and
     preserves shadow witnesses that stay inside one parent block.  Padding a
     single top-level seam by `O(h)` repeated endpoint sets also repairs short
     runs at that seam.  What is not justified is a recursively near-Hamilton
     length bound.  If the padding rule is propagated through the whole
     four-way recursion with the same target bandwidth, the expanded recursion
     tree has `Theta(W(k))` internal block occurrences; `Theta(h)` padding at
     each gives `Theta(h W(k))`, not `o(W(k))`, extra symbols.  Even with
     dimension-dependent bandwidths the accumulated overhead requires a
     separate global estimate and is not shown to be `o(W(k))`.  Thus the
     braid is a useful seed heuristic, not a proof of the wide-row lemma.

140. For the finite targets currently under attack, the erosion proposal does
     not yield exactness.  At `k=14`, even a permutation of all 3432 middle
     sets with complete depth-6 shadows and 7-long runs would produce length
     `3432+12+1=3445`, above the lower bound 3434 (though better than the
     current verified upper bound 3704).  The existing exact search uses delay
     two and flexible sparse pinning precisely to pursue 3434.  The erosion
     direction is therefore most relevant to the asymptotic constant-one
     question, while the fixed-delay central searches remain appropriate for
     exact `k<20` work.

## 27. A dual-path braid giving complete rank-6 shadow at k=14

141. Mining the two complementary `k=13` skeletons gives a deterministic
     construction that removes the first exact `k=14` SAT stage.  Let
     `X=[13]`, and suppose

     * `A_1,...,A_1716` is a Hamilton path through all rank-7 subsets of `X`
       whose 1715 adjacent intersections are distinct, omitting the unique
       rank-6 set `C*`, with `C*` contained in the final endpoint; and
     * `P_1,...,P_1716` is a Hamilton path through the same layer whose
       adjacent unions cover every rank-8 subset of `X`.

     The first path is obtained by cutting Knuth's star-transposition
     middle-levels cycle.  For the second, use the independently found
     rank-8-complete SAT skeleton.  Complementing the latter gives the rank-6
     path

        B_i = X \ P_i,

     whose adjacent intersections cover every rank-5 subset, since

        B_i intersection B_(i+1) = X \ (P_i union P_(i+1)).

142. A three-piece path rearrangement makes the complemented path begin at
     `C*` while preserving Johnson adjacency, its permutation of all rank-6
     sets, and complete rank-5 intersection coverage.  With a new coordinate
     `z`, concatenate

        A_1,...,A_1716,
        z union B_1,...,z union B_1716.

     This is a Hamilton path through all `binom(14,7)=3432` rank-7 sets.  Its
     rank-6 adjacent intersections are complete:

     * the first block gives every rank-6 set in `X` except `C*`;
     * the seam gives exactly `C*`, because the final `A` endpoint is
       `C*+x` while the next vertex is `C*+z`;
     * the second block gives every `z union R`, `|R|=5`.

     Hence all `binom(14,6)=3003` rank-6 masks occur.  The executable
     constructor is `build_k14_two_block_seed.cpp`, and its checked output is
     `k14_two_block_seed.txt`.

143. This is a central skeleton, not yet a length-3434 OR array.  Initially it
     has delay-two factorization deficit 901 and covers 1853/2002 rank-5
     triple intersections.  A hard-color local search preserves all 3003
     rank-6 colors while reducing the run deficit, and exact lazy SAT searches
     now require only run repair plus the remaining rank-5 triples.  A second
     sparse exact formulation takes the union of this braid's edges with the
     square-lift path's edges: the braid supplies complete lower colors, while
     the square lift supplies the interleaved, deficit-zero geometry observed
     in the exact `k=10` and `k=12` paths.

## 28. Pattern audit of every stored optimum

144. Exhaustive shortest-witness analysis of the actual optimal arrays reveals
     a stable structural pattern that is obscured in decimal notation.  For
     `k=9,10,12`, with `r=ceil(k/2)` and `d=nu(k)-binom(k,r)=2`, the row

        T_i = A_i union A_(i+1) union A_(i+2)

     is a permutation of the entire rank-`r` layer and every adjacent pair in
     `T` is a Johnson edge.  All upper union derivatives of `T` are complete.
     At `k=10,12`, its adjacent intersections and triple intersections are
     also complete.  Numerically:

        k=10: 252/252 central sets, 251/251 Johnson edges,
              210/210 rank-4 intersections, 120/120 rank-3 triples;
        k=12: 924/924 central sets, 923/923 Johnson edges,
              792/792 rank-5 intersections, 495/495 rank-4 triples.

145. The factor labels are sparse erosions of this path.  Write

        P_i = A_i union A_(i+1).

     Internally, `P_i` is contained in `T_(i-1) intersection T_i`, and `A_i`
     is contained in the corresponding triple intersection.  In the exact
     `k=12` optimum, all 923 pair envelopes have rank five and all 922 triple
     envelopes have rank four.  Of these, 868 pair labels equal their maximal
     envelope and 503 entries equal their maximal envelope; the remaining
     labels are deliberately shrunk to enumerate the lower masks.  Every mask
     of ranks one through four occurs literally as an entry, every rank-five
     mask first occurs as a pair OR, and 922/924 rank-six masks first occur as
     triple ORs (the other two already occur as pairs).

146. This identifies the recurring construction principle more precisely:

        two-sided shadow-complete Johnson path
          -> maximal intersection erosion
          -> sparse coordinate pins that enumerate the low layers.

     It explains why searching decimal arrays directly is ineffective and why
     the exact `k=14` search is split into (i) central two-sided shadows and
     run factorability, then (ii) sparse factor labeling.  The new hard-color
     search works on the first object and never sacrifices its certified 3003
     rank-6 intersection colors.

## 29. Exact pinnable-row formulation

147. The maximal erosion theorem must be separated from the weaker exact
     factor-labeling problem.  For a prescribed central row `T_1,...,T_M` and
     delay `d`, define

        E_j = intersection { T_i : max(1,j-d) <= i <= min(M,j) }.

     Every factor `D^d A=T` satisfies `A_j subset E_j`.  Assign each lower
     target `S` injectively to an interval `J_S` of length at most `d`.  For
     each coordinate `b`, remove from its envelope positions every interval
     assigned to a target excluding `b`:

        Z_b = {j : b in E_j} \ union {J_S : b notin S}.

     The assignment and central row are simultaneously realizable if and only
     if

        J_S intersects Z_b for every b in S,

     and

        [i,i+d] intersects Z_b for every b in T_i.

     Necessity is immediate.  For sufficiency, put `b` at all positions in
     `Z_b` (or any hitting subset).  Intervals assigned to targets excluding
     `b` contain no occurrence, positive target intervals retain an occurrence,
     and every central window retains every required coordinate.  Bits outside
     a prescribed central mask are already forbidden by the envelopes.

148. This is strictly weaker than demanding that maximal erosion windows equal
     every lower target.  It changes the exact `k=14` workflow: complete
     rank-6 adjacent-intersection envelopes plus run factorability are the
     first gate; complete rank-5 triple intersections are a useful heuristic
     bonus, not a necessary constraint.  Once a deficit-zero path is found,
     solve the injective short-interval assignment and coordinate pin-survival
     problem directly.  A new `lowerbaseruns` exact mode implements this
     relaxed gate, while the older `lowerbaselazy` mode retains the stronger
     triple-intersection ansatz for comparison.

149. The Pascal recursion still needs global cost control.  If `s(k)` physical
     seams each cost `O(h)`, near-width length requires `s(k)h=o(W(k))`.
     Recursively padding `Theta(W(k))` expanded block occurrences costs
     `Theta(hW(k))`.  Only a genuinely cyclic globalization with one final cut,
     or virtual endpoint signatures resolved by one global matching after
     flattening, can avoid this accounting obstruction.  Literal binomial-tail
     formulas must likewise use the nonnegative actual tail count when
     `h>=k/2`, rather than a formally negative symmetric expression.

## 30. Unrestricted k=14 equality: the 3040-term triple core

150. The fixed equation `T=D^2 A` is not known to be necessary for a
     length-3434 solution.  Nevertheless, the unrestricted monotone-band
     normal form plus the exact short-interval slack forces it on almost the
     whole array.  Put `M=binom(14,7)=3432` and choose one witness for every
     rank-7 mask.  In sorted-left-endpoint order write

        I_i=[i+alpha_i,i+beta_i],  0<=alpha_i<=beta_i<=2.

     Every physical interval of length at least three contains some `I_i`, so
     every mask of rank at most six has a singleton or adjacent-pair witness.
     There are 6867 such physical intervals and exactly

        sum_(r=1)^6 binom(14,r)=6475

     lower masks.  After selecting one distinct short witness per lower mask,
     precisely 392 short intervals remain unused by this system.

151. The possible band states are `00,01,02,11,12,22`.  The coordinatewise
     monotonicity of `(alpha_i,beta_i)` makes the state sequence a chain.  Every
     state except `02` is a short interval and therefore consumes one of the
     392 exceptional short intervals.  Hence at least

        3432-392=3040

     rank-7 witnesses have state `02`.  Since `02` and `11` are incomparable,
     state `11` is absent.  Thus every hypothetical optimum has the five-block
     form

        00* 01* 02* 12* 22*,

     and its `02` block is one contiguous fixed-delay triple core of length at
     least 3040.  This is an unconditional statement about the unrestricted
     equality case, not a fixed-row assumption.

152. Select witnesses for ranks six and seven and join a six-set `C` to a
     seven-set `T` by an `L` edge when their intervals share a left endpoint,
     and by an `R` edge when they share a right endpoint.  Each color class is
     a matching, every edge is an inclusion `C subset T`, no pair has both
     colors, and alternating cycles are impossible: along `C -L-> T -R-> C'`
     both interval endpoints strictly increase.  Hence the two-colored graph
     is a spanning linear forest.  Its color matchings each have between 3001
     and 3003 edges, so it has 429--433 components; at least 2999 six-sets and
     at least 2570 seven-sets have degree two.  The identical conclusions hold
     for the rank-7/rank-8 endpoint forest.

153. At most 392 selected rank-6 witnesses are singletons.  Indeed, every
     path edge incident with such a singleton position either duplicates that
     six-set or has rank at least seven, so it is one of the 392 exceptional
     short intervals; a proper vertex subset of a path is incident with at
     least as many edges as vertices.  Removing the at most four non-degree-two
     six-sets, the at most 392 singleton six-sets, and the at most `2*392`
     lower incidences touching a nontriple central witness leaves

        3003-4-392-784=1823

     distinct rank-6 masks that are intersections of consecutive triple-core
     rank-7 masks.  Thus at least 1823 core adjacencies are genuine Johnson
     edges with distinct lower colors.

154. On the upper side, at least `2999-784=2215` rank-8 masks have two triple
     central neighbors.  A rank-8 witness has length at most
     `3434-binom(14,8)+1=432`, so each such mask is the union of two core sets
     whose indices differ by at most 429.  Finally, intersecting the sets of
     lower-degree-two, upper-degree-two, and triple-core seven-sets gives at
     least

        2570+2570+3040-2*3432=1316

     simultaneous Boolean diamonds `C_L union C_R=T=U_L intersection U_R`.
     The remaining unrestricted question is whether the 392 fringe exceptions
     can coexist with complete upper coverage and pinnability, or whether the
     endpoint forests force still more coalescence.

## 32. Corrected closed odd-to-even braid

158. Let `X` have size `2r-1`, let `P_0,...,P_(M-1)` be a Hamilton path of all
     rank-`r` subsets, and put `C_i=P_i intersection P_(i+1)`.  Suppose the
     `C_i` are distinct and omit exactly `C*`, with

        C* subset P_0 intersection P_(M-1).

     For a new coordinate `z`, the forward braid

        P_0,...,P_(M-1), z union C*, z union C_0,...,z union C_(M-2)

     is a Hamilton path through the rank-`r` layer on `X union {z}`.  Its no-z
     lower colors are complete, and its z-containing upper colors are exactly
     all `z union P_i`.  The only remaining first-shadow requirements are

        {P_i union P_(i+1)} = all no-z rank-(r+1) sets,

     and

        {C* intersection C_0} union
        {C_(i-1) intersection C_i : 1<=i<M-1}

     covering every rank-`(r-2)` subset of `X`.  The forward order is essential:
     reversing the `C_i` row duplicates one seam endpoint color and loses the
     other.  This is a proved lift theorem, but the present k=13 source still
     misses some required upper unions/intersections and does not satisfy the
     delay-two run condition.

## 34. Direct factor-word reconnection theorem

168. The SAT factor permits a broader exact search that no longer needs to
     preserve the fixed central-row ansatz.  For a word `A`, horizon `H`, and
     mask `S`, let `c_A(S)` count the intervals of length at most `H` whose OR
     is `S`.  Partition `A` into signed blocks, each of length at least `H`, and
     reorder/reverse the blocks to form `A'`.  If `R(S)` and `N(S)` count the
     old-cut and new-join crossing windows of color `S`, then exactly

        c_(A')(S) = c_A(S) - R(S) + N(S).

     Every short window is either internal to one block, where signed
     permutation gives an OR-preserving bijection, or crosses exactly one
     join.  This proves the formula.  Therefore a move satisfying

        c_A(S)>0  implies  c_A(S)-R(S)+N(S)>0

     for every currently covered `S`, and with `N(Q)>0` for a missing `Q`, is
     a certified monotone coverage improvement.  No factor SAT is required:
     the modified object is the actual array.

169. Every mask covered by `k14_pinnable_factor_16093.txt` has a shortest
     witness of length at most ten.  Taking `H=10`, a join contributes only

        sum_(h=2)^10 (h-1) = binom(10,2) = 45

     crossing windows.  Exact move deltas are therefore constant-size.  A
     segment reversal of whole blocks changes only two joins; a block
     relocation changes three.  Internal joins of a reversed segment are
     preserved because

        J(u,v) = J(reverse(v),reverse(u)).

     Suffix/prefix OR profiles index every target-producing join.  For target
     `Q`, a suffix mask `X subset Q` is compatible precisely with prefixes

        Y = (Q setminus X) union Z,  Z subset X.

     The full proof and move-generator design are in
     `K14_FACTOR_KBREAK_DESIGN.md`.

170. There is also a matching structural explanation for why leaving the
     Johnson component is natural.  The 3432 triple windows give all rank-7
     masks, but their 3431 transitions need only provide 3003 rank-8 masks.
     Hence

        3431 - 3003 = 428

     transitions are surplus.  If two consecutive rank-7 triple values are
     `X,Y` with `|X union Y|=s`, then

        |X intersection Y| = 14-s.

     A non-Johnson transition producing a missing rank-9, rank-10, or rank-11
     mask is therefore naturally paired with a rank-5, rank-4, or rank-3
     shared lower envelope.  There are respectively 378, 2100, and 5775
     unordered rank-7 bridge choices for a fixed upper target.  The 290
     missing upper masks fit inside the 428-transition budget, leaving 138
     filler bridges.  This agrees with the independently forced central
     endpoint-forest picture and explains why insisting on all 3431 Johnson
     edges is unnecessarily rigid.

     neighborhood was likewise empty.

     Repeating the enumeration while protecting only the already complete
     ranks one through eight, allowing arbitrary losses and gains above rank
     eight, again produced no feasible relocation.  Thus the immediate
     obstruction is already the need to recreate the vulnerable rank-7 triple
     colors at the three new seams, rather than preservation of every upper
     color.

     This is an exact exhaustion only for that fixed block partition and move
     family; it is not an impossibility theorem for factor-word repair.  Its
     mathematical implication is that a single coarse block relocation is too
     rigid even after upper-color monotonicity is removed.  The next exact
     neighborhood should coordinate many signed block joins at once (an
     oriented-block path/cycle formulation), or edit a small seam halo in the
     actual factor.  Either route can implement the 428-bridge slack calculation
     of paragraph 170 while collectively restoring all vulnerable rank-7
     windows.

## 35. Exact global normal form: ordered orthogonal chains

173. The all-rank problem has an exact normal form that is more global than a
     derivative row.  Choose one witness interval

        I_S=[l_S,r_S]

     for every nonempty mask S.  For each position p, put

        L_p={S:l_S=p},     R_p={S:r_S=p}.

     The nonempty Boolean lattice is partitioned by the n left families and
     also by the n right families.  Every nonempty family is a chain: intervals
     sharing one endpoint are nested, hence so are their ORs.  The two chain
     partitions are orthogonal,

        |L_p intersect R_q| <= 1,

     because one physical interval [p,q] has only one OR value.  They also
     have forced orders.  Along L_p, rank and right endpoint increase together;
     along R_q, rank increases while left endpoint decreases; and every
     occupied pair satisfies p<=q.

     Thus every solution is an ordered, triangular pair of orthogonal chain
     decompositions of the punctured cube.  This statement uses witnesses for
     every rank simultaneously and is exact, not asymptotic.

174. The converse is also exact.  Given one distinct proposed interval I_S
     for every nonempty S, define, for each bit b,

        Z_b=[n] minus union_(S:not containing b) I_S.

     An array realizing all proposed witnesses exists if and only if

        I_S intersect Z_b is nonempty     for every b in S.

     Necessity is contamination avoidance.  For sufficiency, put b at every
     position of Z_b, or at any hitting subset of Z_b meeting all positive
     intervals.  Negative intervals then contain no b and every positive
     interval contains b.  Coordinates are independent.  Therefore

        universal OR array
          <=> ordered triangular orthogonal chain pair + pin survival.

     Full proofs, including the empty-mask convention, are in
     `GLOBAL_FLAG_RIGIDITY.md`.

175. This reduction connects the problem to established Boolean-lattice
     structure.  Shearer and Kleitman constructed two orthogonal minimum chain
     decompositions for every cube.  Spink constructed three in broad
     dimensions, and Daubel--Jager--Mutze--Scheucher constructed four for
     sufficiently large dimensions.  Hence abstract width-sized orthogonality
     is already available.  The genuinely new requirements here are:

        compatible endpoint orders;
        support in the triangular region p<=q;
        coordinatewise pin survival.

     A plausible route to `nu(k)=B(k)` is therefore to start from a known pair
     of orthogonal symmetric-chain decompositions, refine/split them into the
     `B(k)-W(k)` additional endpoint-chain slots allowed by rank slack, and
     prove that the resulting chains can be ordered and pinned.  The extra
     slots cannot always be empty: for example, at k=6 a pure pair of W(k)
     central-crossing SCD chains has too few lower-band incidence cells, so
     lower chain pieces must occupy the added slots.  This is still one all-k
     construction theorem, unlike repairing one central path at a time.

176. Near the width, the endpoint form is extremely rigid.  For a rank set R,
     put

        D_R=sum_(s in R) (n-binomial(k,s)).

     At least n-D_R positions simultaneously support a selected left-endpoint
     flag through every rank in R, and the same is true on the right.  In each
     rank s in R, at least

        2n-2D_R-binomial(k,s)

     masks lie at the crossing of two such full flags.  For
     n=(1+epsilon_k)W(k), a band of half-width J is almost entirely crossed
     whenever

        J -> infinity,  J=o(k^(1/3)),  J*epsilon_k=o(1).

     At a crossed mask S, the two distinct one-rank upper neighbors supplied
     by the left and right flags uncross to an interval whose OR is their
     rank-|S|+2 union.  Hence Boolean diamonds are forced throughout an
     unbounded central band in every asymptotically width-optimal solution.
     Iterating these diamonds without collisions is the next lower-structure
     question; it is not yet proved.

## 36. Dimension maps and the Catalan correction

177. There is a useful exact restriction map.  If A is universal on X and
     Y is a subset of X, retain exactly those entries A_i contained in Y.
     The resulting subsequence is universal on Y: a witness for S subseteq Y
     could not have contained an entry using a coordinate outside Y.

     If a_s counts weight-s entries of a universal k-word, double counting
     restrictions to ell coordinates gives

        sum_s a_s binomial(k-s,ell-s)
            >= binomial(k,ell) nu(ell).

     In particular, if f_b is the number of entries containing bit b, then

        f_b <= n-nu(k-1),

     and summing over b gives the new rank-distribution inequality

        sum_i |A_i| <= k(n-nu(k-1)).

     These inequalities hold for every array and every ell and give a global
     linear-programming relaxation beyond the middle-antichain count.

178. This theorem explains rigorously why the exact k=12 array does not simply
     solve k=11.  Its coordinate frequencies are

        255,258,251,256,253,252,254,260,265,257,262,285,

     so literal coordinate restrictions have lengths

        671,668,675,670,673,674,672,666,661,669,664,641.

     The best is 641, not 465.  Entrywise join quotients cannot halve the word
     either: a surjective join map from k atoms to k-1 atoms has at most one
     atom in its kernel and automatically deletes only literal occurrences of
     that singleton.

     The correct central reduction retains both coordinate sections.  In a
     two-sided row T, the subsequence avoiding z preserves every union-shadow
     witness whose target avoids z; the containing-z subsequence, after
     erasing z, preserves every intersection-shadow witness whose target
     contains z.  For k=12 these are complementary upper-complete rank-6 and
     lower-complete rank-5 seeds on eleven bits.  Expanding same-section
     Johnson edges by their intersection or union turns the whole k=12 path
     into a spanning alternating walk of the k=11 middle-level incidence
     graph.  Reverse reduction is therefore a repeat-elimination/absorption
     theorem on that walk, not ordinary projection.

179. The parity change contains an exact Catalan term:

        W(2m+1)=2W(2m)-Cat_m,
        Cat_m=W(2m)/(m+1),
        W(2m+2)=2W(2m+1).

     In any length W(2m+1)+d extension, at least Cat_m-d paired masks S and
     {z} union S share a right endpoint, and at least Cat_m-d share a left
     endpoint.  The two families of S are disjoint, because one pair cannot
     share both endpoints.  Thus the Catalan saving is forced endpoint reuse,
     not merely binomial arithmetic.  A sharp even-to-odd recursion must
     interleave these two directed Catalan hook families; every one-interface
     lift has length at least nu(2m)+W(2m) and is too long.

     The full dimension-map proofs and the exact k=12 audit are in
     `DIMENSION_MAPS_HANDOFF.md`.

## 37. A width-plus-k global construction target

180. There is a second clean all-k route through last-occurrence states.  An
     endpoint state is an ordered partition

        Pi=(B_1,...,B_t)

     of the coordinates; its suffix ORs are the prefix unions of the blocks.
     Appending a mask X performs the exact subset move-to-front operation

        M_X(Pi)=(X,B_1 minus X,...,B_t minus X),

     after empty blocks are deleted.

     Call a sequence Pi_1,...,Pi_W an MTF--SCD tour if an SCD chain C_i is
     embedded in the prefix-union chain of Pi_i, every SCD chain occurs once,
     and Pi_(i+1)=M_(X_i)(Pi_i) for one nonempty update mask.  Initializing
     Pi_1 by writing its blocks in reverse costs at most k entries; every later
     state costs one entry.  Therefore the following implication is proved:

        MTF--SCD tour exists  ==>  nu(k)<=W(k)+k-1.

     Since the SCD itself partitions the entire Boolean lattice, this one
     object simultaneously resolves lower pinning and all upper shadows.  It
     would prove the asymptotically optimal leading constant one even in a
     stronger, dynamically flagged form.

181. A concrete Greene--Kleitman one-step transition was audited.  Replacing
     the last two stars of a chain template by 0 and 1 is genuinely exposed by
     one move-to-front update, with block ties handled correctly.  However the
     map is not injective:

        **01  and  01**  both map to 0101.

     In fact its image has size W(k)-W(k-1), so this transition alone leaves
     about half the chains as path starts and does not prove a near-Hamilton
     tour.  The honest remaining lemma is a state-transversal Hamilton-path
     problem: choose one exposing ordered-partition state for every SCD chain
     so consecutive chosen states are related by one subset move-to-front.
     This exact target, proof, and failed-injectivity audit are in
     `GLOBAL_MTF_SCD_HANDOFF.md`.

## 38. Revised research priority

182. The finite k=14 climb is frozen as supporting evidence rather than the
     main program.  The mathematical priorities are now:

        (1) refine, order, and pin an orthogonal SCD pair in B(k) chain slots;
        (2) solve the MTF--SCD state-transversal tour, first asymptotically;
        (3) prove a Catalan-compressed parity braid using the forced endpoint
            hooks and the two complementary central sections;
        (4) use finite-k search only to test or refute one of these structural
            lemmas, not to gain isolated masks.

     None of (1)--(3) is yet a proof of the exact formula.  They are global
     theorems whose success would apply to every k, and they isolate the
     genuinely new combinatorics much more sharply than a single central-row
     repair.

## 39. A general two-sided rainbow forest in every even dimension

183. Let k=2m.  A saturated SCD pairs every rank-(m-1) set S with the
     rank-(m+1) set U two steps above it in the same chain.  If T is the
     intermediate middle set and T' is the other middle set between S and U,
     then the Johnson edge TT' has

        T intersect T' = S,
        T union T' = U.

     As S ranges over its layer, the SCD pairing S->U is a bijection.  Hence
     these edges cover every rank-(m-1) intersection and every rank-(m+1)
     union exactly once.

     For the Greene--Kleitman SCD, orient TT' from the chain middle T to T'.
     In the star template this replaces one star coordinate e_q by the next
     coordinate e_(q+1).  The potential sum_(x in T) x strictly increases, so
     the directed graph is acyclic.  It is therefore a spanning two-sided
     rainbow forest on the W(k) middle sets, with

        binomial(2m,m-1)=W(k)-Cat_m

     edges and exactly

        Cat_m=W(k)/(m+1)

     components.  Its roots are precisely the singleton middle SCD chains.
     The full proof is in `GK_TWO_SIDED_RAINBOW_FOREST.md`.

184. This theorem explains the correct central accounting for all even k.
     A linear middle ordering has W(k)-1 transitions.  The rainbow forest
     spends W(k)-Cat_m of them on the two adjacent layers and leaves exactly
     Cat_m-1 generalized bridges for all outer shadows.  For k=14 this is
     3003 forest edges, 429 components, and 428 bridges--exactly the slack
     previously found by the interval analysis.

     The forest is not automatically a linear forest: several vertices may
     point to one parent.  The next precise lemma is to choose the inclusion
     bijection S->U, or perform alternating colour-preserving exchanges in the
     Greene--Kleitman bijection, so that the induced graph has maximum degree
     two while remaining acyclic.  Once this is done, the Cat_m-1 component
     joins become the recursive resource for covering the farther ranks.

## 40. Global pinning compressed to chain frontiers

185. Pin survival has an exact one-dimensional frontier form.  For a bit b and
     physical position j, let

        H_b(j)=max{q : some selected b-negative interval [p,q] has p<=j},

     with maximum zero when the set is empty.  Then j is a legal pin for b if
     and only if

        H_b(j)<j.

     A selected positive interval [p,q] survives for b exactly when it contains
     such a clean diagonal cut j.  This is just the statement that no selected
     b-negative interval crosses j, but it replaces an exponential union of
     forbidden intervals by one monotone frontier.

186. Along a fixed left-endpoint chain, masks not containing b form an initial
     segment and masks containing b form a final segment.  Consequently all
     pinning constraints for b reduce to the first b-positive interval in each
     left chain.  There are at most n such transition cells per coordinate, so
     the complete exact pin test has only O(kn) essential gates.  Once the
     clean cuts are known, the minimum number of actual occurrences of b is
     obtained by the standard greedy right-endpoint stabbing algorithm.

187. A bare local-diamond condition is not sufficient: even with orthogonality,
     both chain orders, and interval-containment monotonicity, a minimal cover
     of one positive interval by overlapping b-negative intervals can have
     arbitrarily many members.  There is, however, a rigorous sufficient local
     rule.  If interval containment respects mask containment and every two
     overlapping or abutting b-negative selected intervals have a selected
     b-negative hull, then pinning for b follows.  A hypothetical negative
     cover can be merged pairwise to one negative hull containing the positive
     interval, contradicting containment monotonicity.

188. Equivalently, pinning holds exactly when the partial labels extend to a
     Boolean join growth diagram on the whole interval triangle,

        X(p,q)=X(p,q-1) union X(p+1,q),

     with the diagonal values X(p,p) as the array entries.  In fixed delay d,
     this recovers the coordinate-run factorization rule, the lower labeling
     gate, and automatic upper unions in one diagram.  It also identifies

        sigma=d*binomial(k,r)+binomial(d+1,2)
                 -sum_(s<r) binomial(k,s)

     as exactly the number of unused short-band cells available for completing
     the growth diagram.  For k=14,r=7,d=2 this is 392.  Full proofs and
     counterexamples are in `GLOBAL_PINNING.md`.

## 41. Why the canonical orthogonal-SCD construction cannot work

189. For two orthogonal endpoint-chain decompositions, ordering is not a free
