     service operation itself.  The next general target is to prove that any
     coherent full-line packing with linear many long plateaux either admits
     an analogous separator/desert reassignment of cost below `4a^3`, or has
     a quantitatively different transition geometry that pays in the
     complete-line or gap-coarea ledger.

## 199. The three-row rank-strip LP adds no new obstruction

813. A later exploratory LP assigned every short-band cell of lengths one,
     two, and three a rank or a hole and minimized the total hole count.  Its
     reported equality `minimum holes=sigma` for
     `k=11,13,15,17,19,21` is algebraically forced.  If `z_(ell,s)` is the
     normalized mass in physical row `ell` and rank `s`, and `h_ell` is the
     hole mass, then

        sum_s z_(ell,s)+h_ell=(n-ell)/M,
        sum_ell z_(ell,s)=C(k,s)/M.

     Summing the first equations and subtracting the second gives

        sum_ell h_ell=sigma/M                              (199.1)

     at every feasible point.  The exact dual certificate uses multipliers
     `+1` on the row equations, `-1` on the rank equations, and zero on all
     extension inequalities.

814. The LP's one-sided extension cuts are valid rank-profile projections of
     the occupied-band theorem, but exact integer profiles satisfy them in
     all six reported cases.  Therefore the computation proves neither a
     construction nor a stronger lower bound.  Useful leverage requires hole
     locations, both extension directions, the physical join recurrence, or
     pin survival.  The complete audit is
     `RANKSTRIP_LP_TAUTOLOGY_AUDIT.md`.

## 200. Exact two-sided service envelopes and tropical contraction

815. Fix a one-sided span `Lambda`.  An internal threshold run
     `R=[u,v]`, of cost `lambda=v-u`, can serve exactly the left and right
     source intervals

        Omega_R^right=[max(1,v+1-Lambda),u-1],
        Omega_R^left =[v+1,min(M,u-1+Lambda)].              (200.1)

     For a contracted seam `e`, let `kappa_e^right(i)` and
     `kappa_e^left(i)` be the minimum costs of its deleted runs serving `i`
     from the indicated side.  These two functions are the exact service
     state.  When raising a plateau threshold deletes runs `P_j` and merges
     seams `e_j`, the new envelopes are, pointwise,

        kappa_new^epsilon
        =min(kappa_(e_0)^epsilon,...,kappa_(e_s)^epsilon,
             offer_(P_1)^epsilon,...,offer_(P_s)^epsilon). (200.2)

     Thus scalar gaps add ordinarily, while service envelopes compose by
     tropical addition.  Equivalently, the multiplicities of all run offers
     add.  Threshold contraction merely moves a physical run from the
     retained list into a seam; it creates no correction term.

816. Let `q_h(i)` be the minimum of `h` and the cost of every span-`Lambda`
     run serving source `i`.  Choosing a minimizing run, or treating
     `q_h(i)=h` as unassigned, gives

        |S_h|<=sum_i q_h(i)+(2Lambda+h)D.                   (200.3)

     If `C_t` is the union of all source intervals offered by runs of cost at
     most `t`, discrete layer cake gives

        sum_i q_h(i)=hM-sum_(t=0)^(h-1)|C_t|.              (200.4)

     For the three-box middle hexagon, `h=3a-1` and `Lambda=4a+3` yield the
     exact service-volume obstruction

        sum_(t=0)^(3a-2)|C_t|
        <=5a^3+(3/2)a^2-(3/2)a+(11a+5)D.                  (200.5)

     A fractional certificate assigning at most unit mass per source is
     equivalent: its total saving cannot exceed the right side of (200.5).
     These statements were independently cross-audited.  The proof is
     `TWO_SIDED_SERVICE_ENVELOPE.md`.

817. The bookkeeping problem is therefore solved exactly.  What remains is
     geometric: force service volume greater than `(5+epsilon)a^3` in every
     putative subquadratic-defect order, or build a physical order staying at
     or below `5a^3+o(a^3)` while satisfying the complete-line, seam, and
     pinning laws.  This reduction does not assert that the desired strict
     lower bound already holds.

## 201. Consecutive-peak service and the new direction/order bottleneck

818. Let `P_j,P_(j+1)` be consecutive long internal peak runs, with costs
     `lambda_j,lambda_(j+1)` and `g_j` intervening positions.  If their hull
     has one-sided span at most `4a+3`, assign starts in `P_j` to `P_(j+1)`
     and each gap start to the cheaper neighbouring run.  The exact seam cost
     is

        (lambda_j+1)lambda_(j+1)
        +g_j min(lambda_j,lambda_(j+1)).                    (201.1)

     Bad hulls use the universal cost-`2a` assignment.  Shared endpoints and
     word boundaries cost only the explicitly recorded boundary mass.  Span
     alone keeps both endpoint congestions `O(a)`.

819. In a normalized good-seam limit `(p,s,z)` with bad/boundary mass `b`,
     every subquadratic-defect survivor must satisfy

        integral[ps+z min(p,s)]d rho+2b>=4,                (201.2)

     together with

        integral(p+z)d rho+b=3.                            (201.3)

     For a complete fixed-threshold dangerous list, the bad-gap cost can be
     sharpened using the exact deep-gap function rather than the raw `2a`
     fallback.  The theorem and cross-audit are in
     `TWO_SIDED_PEAK_SERVICE.md`.

820. Equations (201.2) and unlabelled complete-line coarea still do not close
     the relaxation.  The diagonal profile

        mu(ds)=2*1_[1,2](s)ds, p=s, z=b=0

     has service moment `14/3` and is statically realized by a family of
     complete parallel lines.  But it is not a physical peak order: two
     consecutive gap-zero blocks on one coordinate cannot both be internal
     peaks.  The next genuinely new theorem must therefore couple **line
     direction to word order**—parallel coarea saturation must create
     valleys/cheap separators or force direction changes.  Another scalar
     moment inequality cannot distinguish this last relaxed survivor.

## 202. Sharp nonabsorbed short-hull service dichotomy

821. Let consecutive dangerous peak plateaux have normalized predecessor
     length `p`, successor length `s`, and strict gap `z`, with

        1<=p,s<=2,  p+s+z<=4.

     If the seam is nonabsorbed, the audited seam-local maximum theorem
     supplies an internal run inside the seam of cost at most `za+O(1)`.
     Assign predecessor-interior starts to the cheaper of this run and the
     successor; assign gap starts to the cheaper neighbouring peak.  The
     leading record cost is

        C_N(p,s,z)=p min(s,z)+z min(p,s).                   (202.1)

     A four-case optimization proves the sharp pointwise inequality

        C_N(p,s,z)<=(4/3)(p+z),                            (202.2)

     with equality only at

        p=s=z=4/3.                                         (202.3)

     All chosen runs have one-sided span at most `4a+3`; shared endpoints
     contribute only `O(a^2)` globally.

822. Split short seams into nonabsorbed and absorbed measures
     `rho_N,rho_A`, and let `b` be normalized bad-hull/boundary mass.  Put

        Delta_N=(4/3)(p+z)-C_N,
        C_A=ps+z min(p,s),
        Delta_A=C_A-(4/3)(p+z).

     The mass identity gives the global assignment bound

        Q/a^3<=4-integral Delta_N d rho_N
                 +integral Delta_A d rho_A+(2/3)b+o(1).    (202.4)

     Absorption requires `p+s<=3`, and exact optimization gives

        Delta_A<=2/3,                                     (202.5)

     uniquely maximized at `(p,s,z)=(1,2,0)`.  Therefore every
     subquadratic-defect survivor must obey

        integral Delta_N d rho_N
        <=(2/3)(||rho_A||+b)+o(1).                         (202.6)

823. At the bottom threshold, if `delta=3-ell`, a bad seam satisfies

        z>(2-p)+(2-s)+o(1).

     Combining line uniqueness near length two with the total gap budget and
     optimizing the split parameter gives

        N_bad/a<=2 sqrt(6delta)+o(1),
        b<=4 sqrt(6delta)+delta+o(1).                       (202.7)

824. Thus all remaining positive excess is localized to exactly three
     sources: absorbed short seams, bad long hulls, or concentration near the
     neutral triple `(4/3,4/3,4/3)`.  The inherited atomic theorem excludes
     mass two at this point, but not every atomic mass.  The exact next theorem
     must jointly charge absorbed positive lines and the bad-hull budget and
     separately resolve the neutral equality case.  The proof and algebra are
     `SHARP_NONABSORBED_SERVICE.md`.

825. The old sharp **scalar** relaxation has a coherent neutral equality
     ledger

        rho=(9/8) delta_(4/3,4/3,4/3), alpha=0, b=0.       (202.8)

     It has edge mass `ell=3/2`, gap mass `3/2`, service cost exactly four,
     and for every `1<c<4/3`

        U(c)=5-3c/4>=4.                                    (202.9)

     Equal direction-line measures on `[-3/16,3/16]` satisfy the unlabelled
     full-line/coarea inequality with slack.  Section 203 below nevertheless
     excludes a physical realization by restoring completeness of the
     dangerous-plateau list.

## 203. Dangerous-list self-closure removes the neutral equality

826. For consecutive `c`-dangerous directed peak plateaux in a nonabsorbed
     seam, the seam-local maximum theorem gives an internal threshold run
     `R` inside the strict seam.  Taking a top-level block of `R` produces an
     internal constant-coordinate peak `Q`.  If `Q` is nondirected, it
     contains a singleton cross-coordinate peak.  If it is directed and has
     cost greater than `ca`, then it is itself a `c`-dangerous plateau lying
     between two allegedly consecutive members of the complete dangerous
     list, a contradiction.  Therefore the seam has an effective run of
     cost

        at most min(g+1,ca).                               (203.1)

     The statement remains valid at shared endpoints, where the seam run is
     already a singleton.

827. The exact physical nonabsorbed saving is consequently

        phi_c^*(p,s,z)
        =min(p,(4-s-z)_+) [s-min(c,z)],                    (203.2)

     rather than the former

        min(p,(4-s-z)_+) (s-z)_+.

     All safe-source, span, congestion, and boundary arguments are unchanged.
     On a short hull the record cost becomes

        C_(N,c)=p min(c,z)+z min(p,s).                     (203.3)

828. At the former neutral triple `(4/3,4/3,4/3)`, any fixed `c<4/3`
     gives a strict additional saving.  The mass-`9/8` ledger has

        Q(c)/a^3<=2+(3/2)c+o(1)<4.                         (203.4)

     Thus it cannot arise from a physical subquadratic-defect middle order;
     it survived only because the scalar relaxation forgot a newly exposed
     dangerous run.  Three independent audits found no maximality,
     shared-endpoint, or list-order defect.  The theorem is
     `DANGEROUS_LIST_SELF_CLOSURE.md`.

829. The remaining broad obstruction is now reduced to absorbed seams and
     bad long-hull mass.  The next optimization must use the strengthened
     `phi_c^*` jointly with direction-labelled positive-line geometry and the
     bad-gap budget at one common threshold.

## 204. Uniform margin removes the entire neutral branch

830. Fix `1<c<4/3`.  On every nonabsorbed short-hull record

        p,s>=c,  z>=0,  p+s+z<=4,

     dangerous-list self-closure gives the cost

        C_c(p,s,z)=p min(c,z)+z min(p,s).

     A complete case optimization, independently audited, proves the sharp
     uniform inequality

        (4/3)(p+z)-C_c(p,s,z)
        >=K(c):=(4/3-c)(2-c)>0.                       (204.1)

     Equality is unique at

        p=s=(4-c)/2,  z=c.                            (204.2)

831. Let `m_N` be nonabsorbed short-seam mass, `rho_A` absorbed short-seam
     mass, and `b` bad-hull/boundary **word mass**.  Put

        E=||rho_A||+b.

     The service lower bound and the absorbed excess `Delta_A<=2/3` imply

        K(c)m_N<=(2/3)E+o(1).                         (204.3)

     Since every short record has `p+z<=4-c`, the word-mass identity also
     gives

        3<=(4-c)(m_N+E)+o(1).                         (204.4)

     Consequently every subquadratic-defect survivor must satisfy

        E>=3K(c)/[(4-c)(K(c)+2/3)]-o(1).              (204.5)

832. At `c=13/12`, (204.5) is the explicit bound

        E>=396/1505-o(1)=0.26312...-o(1).

     As `c` decreases to one, the lower bound tends to `1/3`.  Hence the
     former neutral concentration is not merely excluded pointwise: every
     remaining process must move a positive amount of mass into absorbed
     seams or bad long hulls.

833. This is the current exact frontier.  The remaining theorem must charge
     the mandatory mass in (204.5) against the positive-line/coarea energy
     of absorbed successors and the direction-labelled bad-gap budget at the
     **same threshold**.  The proof is `UNIFORM_SHORT_HULL_MARGIN.md`.

## 205. Independent audit of Fable's full-line-deficit note

834. Fable's `FABLE_FULL_LINE_DEFICIT_RESOLUTION.md` has one valid new
     contribution.  If `gamma_des` is normalized word mass at middle-hexagon
     points outside the selected complete-line union, then

        D_a/a^2=gamma_des+o(1),  gamma_des<=delta,

     and the fixed-bottom wedge calculation sharpens to

        U(1+)<=15/4+(5/4)sqrt(6 gamma_des)
                       +3 gamma_int-(3/2)delta
              <=15/4+(5/4)sqrt(6 gamma_des)+(3/2)delta.    (205.1)

     Hence every profile with

        gamma_des<(1-6delta)^2/150,  delta<1/6             (205.2)

     is excluded.  The gap partition is valid after defining the terminal
     mass to include both linear end gaps.  The level-tension bathtub bounds
     in its Lemma 6.1 are also correct.

835. The note's Theorem 7.1 is not proved.  The baseline change from threshold
     one to `c` is

        3(c-1)+2(e(c)-e(1)),

     not `3c-3+2e(c)`; its derivative `3-2f(c)` may be negative.  Thus
     monotonicity of `delta(c)` and `gamma_des(c)` does not imply
     bottom-threshold optimality, and the claim that no threshold sweep can
     help must be retracted.

836. The proposed scalar extremizer is internally inconsistent.  Under its
     sharp `(2,2,1)` gap interpretation and the crossing equality `C=2A`,
     its total `p+s` moment is at least six, whereas the required moment is
     `6-2delta`.  The two agree only at `delta=0`.  Therefore it does not
     prove sharpness of the six-family relaxation.

837. Fable's Lemma M remains unproved and uses `gamma_cov` inconsistently.
     Its conditional reduction is algebraically valid (with constant `12.5`,
     not `12`, at `delta_1=1/24`), but its claimed uniqueness/minimality is
     obsolete after the stronger self-closed saving (203.2).  The independent
     audit is
     `fable_general_case/FABLE_FULL_LINE_DEFICIT_INDEPENDENT_AUDIT.md`.

## 206. Sharp absorbed/bad bounds and the missing drift coupling

838. If an absorbed seam uses a successor line at normalized positive level
     `t`, then `p<=1+t` and `s<=2-t`.  Exact optimization gives

        g(t):=max Delta_A
        =2/3-t/3-t^2                  (0<=t<=1/3),
         1/3+2t/3-t^2                 (1/3<=t<=1/2),
         4/3-4t/3-t^2                 (1/2<=t<=2/3),
         2/3-t                        (2/3<=t<=1).    (206.1)

     Since the three direction-labelled successor measures are each
     dominated by Lebesgue measure, total absorbed mass `A` satisfies

        integral Delta_A<=3 integral_0^(A/3) g(t)dt
                        <=(2/3)A-A^2/18.              (206.2)

     At threshold `c<4/3`, the simpler sharp pointwise bound is

        Delta_A<=c(5/3-c).                            (206.3)

839. Direction labels sharpen the bad-hull count.  If `B` is normalized bad
     seam count and `delta=3-ell`, endpoint-level incidence and a bathtub
     argument give

        B<=sqrt(6delta),
        b<=2sqrt(6delta)+delta+o(1),                  (206.4)

     where `b` is bad-record word mass.  This halves the constants of the
     earlier unlabelled estimate.

840. The scalar system obtained from (206.1)--(206.4) has a saturated
     boundary candidate at

        A_*=1.70817256009...,
        f=(A_*+3)/2,

     where `A_*` is the root in `(3/2,2)` of

        4A^3+24A^2-216A+279=0.                       (206.5)

     It is not a coherent seam process.  Equality forces all three direction
     measures to fill `[0,A_*/3]` and creates absorbed length drift

        integral(s-p)=3/4.

     The remaining seam mass is only

        (3-A_*)/2=0.64591371995...,

     which cannot cancel that drift because `|s-p|<=1`.  This is the first
     use of equality of the complete predecessor and successor **length
     marginals**, rather than their separate scalar moments.

841. This kills only the saturated boundary candidate.  The exact remaining
     theorem must optimize absorbed benefit jointly with absorbed length
     drift and charge the compensating drift to nonabsorbed/bad records.
     The proof ledger is `ABSORBED_BAD_DRIFT_FRONTIER.md`.

## 207. Strategic correction: the primary positive route is four-dimensional

842. The current three-box seam program is a **no-go** program.  It assumes
     a local word of width plus `o(a^2)` and seeks a contradiction.  Closing
     its last mixed/absorbed case would show that the three-box product route
     cannot deliver constant one; it would not construct Boolean-cube words
     and would not strengthen the original Boolean lower bound, because the
     product aggregation implication is one-way.

843. The shortest credible positive all-dimensional target is instead the
     uniform four-box estimate

        g_4(ell)<=w(ell)+O((1+||ell||_1)^(3-epsilon))       (207.1)

     for one fixed `epsilon>0`, including unbalanced and degenerate height
     vectors.  The proved fixed-dimensional aggregation theorem then gives

        nu(k)=W(k)+o(W(k)).                                 (207.2)

844. Existing constructions handle the thin four-box sector and already
     give exact central enumeration with only `O(S^2)` first-shadow defects.
     Their failure is the accumulated deep-tail repair.  The new positive
     target is a global hook-index tail-flow: pair complementary lower/upper
     tail demands, order and orient central-diagonal blocks along monotone
     demand trails, and realize every nonterminal tail by an interval crossing
     the corresponding consecutive block segment.

845. A sufficient intermediate theorem is that this signed hook-index demand
     be packed into one row with `O(S^2)` occurrence overload.  The route
     decision is `GENERAL_ROUTE_DECISION_20260723.md`; Section 208 records
     the factor/pinning correction required before this becomes a max-word.

## 208. Exact correction to the four-box tail-flow target

846. For a fixed hook difference parameter `c` and `R=m-c`, a spanning
     triangular word of length `|T_R|+rho(R)` supplies every residual upper
     tail as a consecutive join.  Its reflected reverse supplies the lower
     tails as consecutive **meets**.  The exact total middle-occurrence count
     over all hook orientations is

        M_m+2rho(m)+4 sum_(R=0)^(m-1)rho(R)+O(m).       (208.1)

     The `O(m)` term permits unmerged sector endpoints and disappears for
     completion-core endpoint conventions.  Thus `rho(R)=O(R)` would indeed
     give only `O(m^2)` tail-shadow overload.

847. This shadow statement is not yet a four-box max-word.  An arbitrary
     triangular order may destroy the natural central-square intervals;
     lower meets are not ORs; an abstract trail count does not bound physical
     cell reuse; and hook-index monotonicity alone does not prevent a
     cross-block entry from exceeding a target.

848. A correct sufficient theorem asks for one row `T_1,...,T_L`,
     `L<=M_m+O(m^2)`, whose intervals give every upper point by joins and
     every lower point by meets, together with monotone linked central
     witness intervals

        I_i=[i+alpha_i,i+beta_i]

     in `N=L+O(m^2)` positions.  If every central positive bit has a legal
     pin and each lower meet `[u,v]` has a nonempty core

        J_(u,v)=[v+alpha_v,u+beta_u]

     retaining every bit of the meet, then the maximal factor is one legal
     max-word of length `N`.  This is exactly the variable-band core-pinning
     theorem.

849. Therefore the positive target is a **factorable triangular braid**:
     near-once triangular packing, central-square compatibility, linked band,
     and simultaneous lower-core pins.  The complete audit and sufficient
     theorem are `FOUR_BOX_POSITIVE_ROUTE_AUDIT.md`.

850. The central-square gap is witnessed already at `R=6`.  The verified
     excess-five triangular word, its reflected reverse, and the six missing
     block centers retain every residual tail shadow but miss 143 upper and
     143 lower central-square targets in the balanced sector.  Hence tail
     universality can actively destroy the diagonal shadow system; this is
     not a merely formal caveat.

## 209. Exact absorbed benefit--drift frontier

851. The saturated absorbed scalar candidate at

        A_*=1.70817256009...,
        4A_*^3+24A_*^2-216A_*+279=0,

     remains impossible even after optimally trading absorbed benefit for
     marginal drift.  Put `N=(3-A)/2` and

        r=(3-A)(2A-3)/(12A),
        u=(2A^2+9A-9)/(12A).

     The exact drift-constrained optimizer has total level density `3 dt`
     on `[r,u]`, marks `p=1+t,s=2-t`, and gaps zero below `t=1/3` and one
     above it.  Its drift is exactly `N`.

852. Its maximum absorbed benefit is

        V(A)=-(8A^5+36A^4+162A^3-1575A^2+324A+729)
              /(864A^2).                                (209.1)

     At `A_*`,

        V(A_*)=0.8262062041...<2(3-A_*)/3
                                =0.8612182933....       (209.2)

     The exact gap `0.0350120891...` is positive by reduction modulo the
     defining cubic.  Thus equality of predecessor and successor length
     marginals eliminates the candidate, not merely its pointwise maximizing
     representative.

853. Scalar drift still cannot close every profile.  The already-audited
     nested alternating-pair broad process satisfies marginal stationarity,
     the three separate line-density caps, contraction, gaps, and the
     self-closed saving, with `U(c)>4` at every threshold.  It fails only the
     complete selected-line intersection inequality: at the bottom,

        ell=3, f=2, tau=1, iota>=1/4

     would force `3<=2f-tau-iota<=11/4`.

854. Therefore the last three-box no-go ingredient must use the full
     cross-direction line-intersection/additive-triple geometry or an
     equivalent direction--word-order theorem.  The Pareto calculation and
     scope are `ABSORBED_DRIFT_PARETO.md`.

## 210. Audit of the three-row rank-strip LP

855. The reported computations `minimum holes = sigma` for odd
     `k=11,13,...,21` are forced by the LP equalities and contain no optimized
     information.  If `z_(ell,s)` counts selected cells of length `ell+1`
     and rank `s`, and `h_ell` is the hole count in that row, the row and rank
     equations are

        sum_s z_(ell,s)+h_ell=(n-ell)/M,
        sum_ell z_(ell,s)=C(k,s)/M.

     Summing the first family and subtracting the second forces

        sum_ell h_ell=sigma/M

     at every feasible point.  The exact dual certificate uses multiplier
     `+1` on each row equality, `-1` on each rank equality, and zero on every
     extension inequality.

856. The extension inequalities are valid coarse necessary conditions, but
     feasibility merely says that the one-sided rank-profile projection sees
     no contradiction.  It is neither a construction nor evidence for the
     exact formula.  A useful relaxation must retain physical hole locations,
     both extension directions, the join recurrence, or coordinate pins.
     The complete audit is `RANKSTRIP_LP_TAUTOLOGY_AUDIT.md`.

## 211. Four-box intact-block barrier and square carrier

857. The proposed monotone transport of residual tails through trails of
     intact central-diagonal blocks is impossible.  The join of every complete
     block has coordinate 2 or 4 equal to `m`, whereas an interior upper tail
     with `c,u>0` has both coordinates strictly below `m`.  Dually, the meet
     of a complete block has coordinate 1 or 3 equal to zero, whereas an
     interior lower tail has both positive.  Hence every bulk tail witness in
     an intact-block concatenation crosses at most one seam.

858. This affects an asymptotic fraction one of the tails.  Their exact count
     in one orientation is

        m(m+1)(m-1)(m-2)/12,

     versus total `m(m+1)^2(m+2)/12`.  A seam supplies only the join grid of
     one suffix chain and one prefix chain, of size at most `(2m+1)^2`; thus
     at least `(1/48+o(1))m^2` seams must be active.  The correct carrier is a
     quadratically productive seam grid, not a multi-block unit-demand trail.

859. For fixed sector `c`, `R=m-c`, all middle cells are exactly the square

        X_c(a,b)=(c+a,m-c-b,b,m-a),  (a,b) in [0,R]^2.

     Consecutive joins and meets are determined by the same axis-aligned
     bounding rectangle of their `(a,b)` points.  The triangular tails are
     only bottom-anchored rectangles; the destroyed central squares are the
     omitted rectangle classes.  This gives a cleaner positive shadow target:
     a near-spanning rectangle word, followed by one linked variable-band
     factor with simultaneous lower pins.

860. If the triangular repetition excess satisfies merely
     `q(R)=O(R^(2-epsilon))`, exact sector accounting already gives subcubic
     shadow overhead.  The remaining tasks are that relaxed all-`R`
     triangular/rectangle construction and the common factor/pinning bridge.
     Proofs and scope are `FOUR_BOX_INTACT_BLOCK_BARRIER.md`.

## 212. The isolated full-square target is quadratically overstrong

861. The square reparametrization in item 859 is exact, but demanding every
     rectangle inside every sector cannot be the positive construction.  An
     elementary two-point rectangle forces its grid edge to occur as one
     consecutive word transition.  Since the `(R+1)`-square grid has

        E_R=2R(R+1)

     edges, any full-square rectangle word has length at least `E_R+1`, and
     hence excess at least `R^2` over its `(R+1)^2` compulsory points.

862. For `R>=2`, the grid has `4(R-1)` odd-degree vertices.  If `d` grid
     edges are repeated and `x` non-grid transitions split the grid-edge
     subsequence into at most `x+1` trails, parity gives

        4(R-1)-2d<=2(x+1).

     Therefore the word length is at least

        2R(R+1)+2R-2,

     and the excess is at least `R^2+2R-3`.  Summing this over sector radii
     already costs `Theta(m^3)`, so isolated square universality cannot prove
     a subcubic four-box error.

863. The genuine triangular demand avoids this barrier: its only elementary
     rectangles are the `R` edges of the bottom peak spine.  Moreover sector
     providers occur in shear-equivalence classes.  For

        X_c(a,b)=(c+a,m-c-b,b,m-a)

     and `Q=[A,B]x[C,D]`, legal shifts satisfy

        J(c,Q)=J(c+t,[A,B-t]x[C-t,D]),
        M(c,Q)=M(c+t,[A-t,B]x[C,D-t]).

     In the bulk, a horizontal elementary edge in sector `c` has the same
     upper color as a vertical edge in sector `c+1` and the same lower color
     as a vertical edge in sector `c-1`.  Requiring both is precisely the
     false factor-two edge demand.

864. The corrected target is a transversal of these sheared provider
     classes, retaining only one representative of each upper and lower
     target, while preserving the natural diagonal intervals and the common
     factor pins.  The proof and correction are
     `SQUARE_RECTANGLE_EDGE_BARRIER.md`.  This section supersedes any reading
     of item 859 that asks for all rectangles separately in each sector.

## 213. Exact limit of the triangular shear quotient

865. Let an upper four-box target `z` have rank `2m+d`, and sort its
     coordinates as `a<=b<=c<=e`.  Even allowing all 24 coordinate
     permutations, it has a bottom-anchored triangular representative if and
     only if

        a<d  and  c+e>m+a.                              (213.1)

     When (213.1) holds, a canonical representative uses roles
     `(c,e,a,b)`, sector `s=m-e`, and rectangle

        [m-b,c+e-m] x [0,a].                           (213.2)

     The lower criterion follows by complement: for sorted lower target
     coordinates it is `e>m-d` and `e>a+b`.

866. This is a volumetric, not boundary, obstruction.  For
     `1<=d<=m/3`, every upper target with all four coordinates at least `d`
     is non-triangularizable.  Its exact depth-`d` count is

        C(2m-3d+3,3)-4C(m-2d+2,3),

     and summing gives

        (245/1944)m^4+O(m^3).

     The same leading term remains if degenerate `u=r` providers are added.
     Hence the shear quotient cannot eliminate the central/non-bottom
     provider system; the target-level decomposition is inherently hybrid.
     The complete classification is
     `FOUR_BOX_SHEAR_QUOTIENT_CLASSIFICATION.md`.

## 214. Intact central diagonals force cubic natural-core slack

867. Let a middle row have length `M_m+E`, preserve every natural central
     diagonal as an intact insertion-free block, and use a monotone factor
     band of slack `d`.  In every block `D_(H,r)`, `1<=r<=H<=m`, the atom
     `(4,m)` occurs at one rare endpoint.  The `2r` successive natural lower
     prefix/suffix meets have distinct spans `1,...,2r`.

868. If `t_B` of those targets are not translated through their natural
     cores, put `T=sum_B t_B`.  Combining exact run factorability, core
     nonemptiness, disjoint alpha/beta offset charging, and the bound on total
     occurrences of `(4,m)` gives

        2d >= m(m+1)(2m+7)/6
              -T-(m+1)(m+2)-2E-(10m+5).              (214.1)

     Therefore `E,d=O(m^2)` forces `T=Omega(m^3)`.  Adding only `O(m^2)`
     literal central repairs cannot rescue the construction.

869. This is an architectural theorem, not an unrestricted lower bound for
     `g_4`.  It is escaped by splitting/interleaving most diagonals, replacing
     a cubic family of natural lower witnesses, or using genuinely non-core
     pin windows.  The audited proof is
     `FOUR_BOX_INTACT_DIAGONAL_CORE_OBSTRUCTION.md`.

## 215. Triangular layer corridors require unbounded sharing

870. For `2<=s<=R` and `1<=d<=s-1`, the target

        [s-1,s] x [0,s-d]

     forces its witness to contain `P_(s-1)` or `P_s`.  If separate defect
     layers `d` use disjoint corridors, the peaks in corridor `d` form a
     vertex cover of the path `d--...--R`, so the total peak count is at least

        sum_(d=1)^(R-1) ceil((R-d)/2)
          =ceil((R^2-1)/4).

     The repetition excess is consequently quadratic.

871. More generally, if one peak occurrence serves at most `C` defect layers
     on either incident row pair, then

        P>=R(R-1)/(4C).

     Thus `O(R log R)` excess requires some portals to serve
     `Omega(R/log R)` different layers.  Fixed-layer, bounded-congestion, and
     naive block concatenations are excluded; a positive braid must encode
     span and height jointly in one two-chain portal grid.  See
     `TRIANGULAR_LAYER_CORRIDOR_BARRIER.md`.

## 216. Portal-master superposition and its residual obstruction

872. The right arms of all triangular portal gadgets do superpose with zero
     repetition.  With peak `P_v` and edge states `E_(v,x)`, the word

        Q_R=B_0B_1...B_R,
        B_v=P_v,E_(v,2),...,E_(v,v-1),

     contains, for every `u`, a prefix ending at `E_(u,x)` (or at the
     appropriate diagonal state) whose rectangle is exactly

        [u,max(u,x+1)] x [0,x].

     All height-one left arms likewise superpose in one descending corridor.
     The intermediate blocks are harmless fillers, so the earlier apparent
     separate-arm cost was not intrinsic.

873. The difficulty is identifying the two monotone masters.  Direct
     identification forces quadratic repetition.  A one-copy Euler cactus
     splice pairs each branch in precisely the way that destroys the desired
     fork.  If every endpoint `u` retains one distinguished portal and the
     portals are arranged by an arbitrary min-Cartesian tree of height `h`,
     then the low-layer repetition is at least

        R(R-1)/(2h)-2R.

     Thus even a balanced tree costs `Omega(R^2/log R)`.  A subquadratic
     solution must split one endpoint across several portals or let one
     portal serve many endpoints.  The construction, proof, and checker are
     `PORTAL_GRID_MASTER_SUPERPOSITION.md` and
     `scratch/verify_portal_master_superposition.py`.

## 217. Higher-dimensional aggregation escape

874. For a fixed `t`-box of total side sum `S`, an estimate

        g_t=w_t+e_t,             e_t=o(S^(t-1))

     uniformly in the side lengths is sufficient for asymptotic Boolean
     constant one.  In particular, a five-box theorem `g_5=w_5+o(S^4)` is
     enough; the formerly targeted `O(S^3)` error is stronger than needed.
     More flexibly, estimates

        g_t <= (1+epsilon_t)w_t+O_t(S^(t-2)),
        epsilon_t -> 0,

     for arbitrarily large fixed `t` also imply `nu(k)=(1+o(1))W(k)`.

875. Standard slicing, SCD connectors, Cartesian products, and complement
     bridges retain a critical-order loss.  A concrete sufficient innovation
     is the shared-initialization suspension

        g(P x [0,h]) <= g(P)+h w(P)+O(S^(dim(P)-1)).

     Iterating it gives leading ratio `sqrt(t/(t-1))`, which tends to one as
     `t` grows.  Hence a proof need not perfect the four-box construction:
     it may instead amortize initialization across increasingly many fixed
     coordinates.  See `HIGHER_DIMENSION_AGGREGATION_ESCAPE.md`.

## 218. Direct two-central-layer trail construction

876. Put `L_s(m)={x in [0,m]^4: sum x_i=s}` and `M_m=|L_(2m)(m)|`.
     There is a word of length

        M_m+O(m^2)

     whose entries are all in `L_(2m-1)(m)`, which contains every point of
     that lower layer literally and whose adjacent coordinatewise maxima
     contain every point of `L_(2m)(m)`.

877. The construction makes `L_(2m-1)` the vertex set of a graph.  For each
     `z in L_(2m)`, choose the edge joining `z-e_1` and `z-e_2` when
     `z_1,z_2>0`, and otherwise join two arbitrary positive-coordinate lower
     covers.  Every nonboundary lower vertex has degree exactly two.  After
     deleting the boundary `v_1 in {0,m}` or `v_2 in {0,m}`, the graph is at
     most one path for every fixed `(v_3,v_4)`.  It therefore has only
     `O(m^2)` components, odd vertices, and isolates.  Euler-trail
     linearization costs only `O(m^2)` beyond its `M_m` coloured edges.

878. More generally, in every fixed dimension `t>=3`, the two adjacent
     layers at any rank `r>m` of `[0,m]^t` have such a word of length

        |L_r^(t)(m)|+O_t(m^(t-2)).

     This is the first proved near-width factor bridge in the four-box route
     that avoids intact blocks and one-portal-per-endpoint rigidity.  It does
     not yet cover all other ranks.  The proof, finite checker, and independent
     audit are `FOUR_BOX_TWO_LAYER_TRAIL.md`,
     `scratch/verify_four_box_two_layer_trail.py`, and
     `TWO_LAYER_TRAIL_INDEPENDENT_AUDIT.md`.

## 219. Exact direct line word and its upper cone

879. The trail theorem has a simpler exact variant if the boundary middle
     points may occur literally.  In a rectangular four-chain box, fix rank
     `r` and, for every transverse pair `(c,d)`, list the whole rank-`r-1`
     line

        (L,K-L,c,d),...,(U,K-U,c,d),
        K=r-1-c-d,
        L=max(0,K-a_2), U=min(a_1,K).

     Concatenate the nonempty lines and append literally the rank-`r` points
     with first or second coordinate zero.  If `m_r` is the rank size and
     `C_r` the number of nonempty transverse lines, the resulting word has
     the exact length

        m_r+C_r <= m_r+(a_3+1)(a_4+1).

     It covers rank `r-1` by singletons and rank `r` by singletons or
     adjacent maxima.

880. For `[0,m]^4` at `r=2m`, every transverse line except `(m,m)` is
     nonempty.  Hence

        C_(2m)=(m+1)^2-1

     and the exact length is

        M_m+m^2+2m.

     This is strictly shorter and more explicit than the arbitrary
     boundary-edge trail, though the latter retains the stronger property
     that every entry lies in rank `2m-1`.

881. All longer within-line maxima are classified.  An interval from
     parameter `p` to `q` has maximum `(q,K-p,c,d)`.  A target `y` of rank
     `r-1+s` occurs in that line exactly when

        L+s <= y_1 <= U.

     In the equal middle cube this is equivalent to `y_1,y_2>=s`.  The
     missed part of depth `s` has size at most `2s(m+1)^2`; consequently one
     spine plus literal exceptions covers any shallow band of depth
     `q=o(sqrt(m))` in `M_m+o(m^3)` positions.  The outstanding problem is
     to superpose changing coordinate-pair directions, rather than repeat
     the width-scale spine for successive bands.  The proof and exhaustive
     rectangular-box checker are `FOUR_BOX_DIRECT_LINE_WORD.md` and
     `scratch/verify_four_box_direct_line_word.py`.

## 220. Multilayer reach and exact limits of the direct line spine

882. Adding the three-box slice words for `x_1=a` and `x_2=a`,
     `0<=a<q`, to the exact line spine covers every rank from `2m-1`
     through `2m-1+q` in length

        M_m+m^2+2m+2q(m+1)(2m+1).

     Consequently every sublinear-depth upper band `q=o(m)` already has a
     width-plus-`o(m^3)` construction.  The unresolved obstruction begins at
     genuinely linear depth, not at a fixed or square-root depth.

883. A target `y` of rank `2m-1+s` lies in some rank-`2m-1`
     coordinate-pair line interval exactly when at least two coordinates of
     `y` are at least `s`.  The targets failing all six pair directions form
     a positive-volume hard family

        H_m={y: #{i:y_i>=s}<=1},
        |H_m|=(1/12)m^4+O(m^3).

     In deficit coordinates `u_i=m-y_i`, sorted increasingly, the condition
     is exactly `u_1+u_3+u_4<=m`; its ordered polytope has volume `1/288`,
     and the 24 permutations give `1/12`.

884. A disjoint tiling of one transverse slice by complete complementary
     pair lines must use all rows or all columns; rows and columns cannot
     coexist because each intersects every member of the other family.  Its
     total within-line interval capacity, maximized independently in every
     slice, is exactly

        m(m+1)(m+2)(m+3)/4=(1/4)m^4+O(m^3).

     Thus, conditional on such a tiling being the chosen upper spine, a
     leading-order family needs cross-block witnesses.  If hard witnesses
     are confined to one line or two adjacent intact lines, at least
     `(1/12-o(1))m^2` seams must change coordinate-pair direction.

885. The literal fixed-pair construction itself still misses

        (1/72)m^4-O(m^3)

     upper targets, in every ordering and orientation of its intact lines.
     The counted subfamily has a unique qualifying coordinate, equal to 1
     or 2.  It contains no complete line; same-pair seams supply only
     `O(m^3)` values, and intervals ending in the `O(m^2)` literal tail
     supply only `O(m^3)` further values because each endpoint contributes
     one coordinatewise chain of length at most `4m+1`.

886. The same intact spine cannot be repaired by a uniform erosion.  Every
     seam between two nontrivial same-pair lines creates an internal
     coordinate-atom run of length at most two, so `T=D^dA` is impossible
     for `d>=2`.  Conversely, if `A` also covers the whole lower half, short
     interval counting forces

        d>=(3/4-o(1))m.

     The surviving target is therefore a surface-scale mixed-direction
     braid with nonlocal portals and genuinely variable central witness
     widths.  The proofs and independent audit are
     `LINE_WORD_MULTILAYER_EXTENSION.md` and
     `LINE_WORD_MULTILAYER_EXTENSION_AUDIT.md`.

## 221. Lexicographic central graph passes every upper target

887. Let `V_m` and `Z_m` be the ranks `2m-1` and `2m` of `[0,m]^4`.
     For every `z in Z_m`, join the two lower covers obtained by subtracting
     from the first two positive coordinates of `z`.  This gives one edge
     coloured `z`, and its endpoint maximum is exactly `z`.

888. This fixed edge selection is simultaneously valid for every upper
     target at the connected-path level.  More generally, let `|y|>=s` and
     `y_i<=s-1`, and consider the selected-cover graph on rank `s-1` below
     `y`.  Start with the reverse-greedy point of mass `s-1`, filling
     coordinates from last to first.  Then process coordinates from its
     first support position down to 1.  To raise coordinate `i`, move one
     unit from the first later positive coordinate `q`.  The corresponding
     rank-`s` point has `i,q` as its first two positive coordinates, so this
     is a selected edge below `y`.

889. The resulting path visits the facet `v_i=y_i` for every coordinate.
     Earlier visited facets may later donate mass, which is harmless.  Every
     move strictly decreases `sum_i i v_i`, so the path is simple.  Taking
     `s=2m` proves that for every `y in [0,m]^4`, `|y|>=2m`, the induced
     selected graph below `y` contains a path whose coordinatewise maximum
     is exactly `y`.

890. Connectivity is not yet interval coverage.  A trail word represents
     `y` exactly when one maximal consecutive run of vertices below `y`
     meets all four facets.  The selected graph has maximum degree three;
     explicitly, if `p<q` are the first two positive positions of a lower
     vertex `v`, then

        deg(v)=q-2+1_(v_p<m)+1_(v_q<m)<=3.

     All degree-not-two vertices, isolates, and graph components number only
     `O(m^2)`.  Thus all internal transitions except a surface-order family
     are forced.

891. The initially proposed upper theorem was the lexicographic excursion
     lemma: choose the transitions at those `O(m^2)` branch vertices so that
     every upper induced graph retains one facet-spanning consecutive
     excursion inside a transition trail.  Section 222 below refutes this
     statement for every `m>=2`.  The reverse-greedy connected-path theorem
     remains valid; the corrected target must allow virtual transitions
     across the seams between oriented trail pieces.

892. Keeping the natural coordinate lines intact cannot prove the desired
     combined central-and-upper word.  Under the additional requirement
     that the lower central layer is also covered, the facet targets
     `(a,0,c,d)` with
     `m/4<=R=2m-1-c-d<=m/2` and `R<a<=m` each force a distinct seam.  Their
     number is

        (11/192+o(1))m^3.

     Hence any intact-line-block word covering all ranks at least `2m-1`
     has length at least

        M_m+(11/192+o(1))m^3.

     The successful transition system must split or splice the lines at
     their surface junctions.  See `CENTRAL_EULER_UPPER_UNIVERSALITY.md`,
     `CENTRAL_EULER_UPPER_UNIVERSALITY_AUDIT.md`, and
     `scratch/check_induced_deficit_components.py`.

## 222. Four-target obstruction and the seam-aware lexicographic target

893. The within-one-transition-trail lexicographic excursion lemma is false
     for every `m>=2`.  Three degree-three vertices

        a=(0,m-1,0,m), b=(0,m-1,1,m-1), c=(0,m,0,m-1)

     support four rank-`2m+1` targets whose necessary transition clauses are

        (xu)_a or (uv)_c,
        (sv)_b,
        (ur)_a or (uw)_c,
        (vt)_b or (vw)_c.

     The second clause forces `(vw)_c`; the first and third then force both
     `(xu)_a` and `(ur)_a`, impossible at the degree-three vertex `a`.  Every
     proper three-clause subfamily is satisfiable, so this is a minimal local
     obstruction.

894. This refutes only the pure rotation-system formulation.  Once the
     transition trails are cut, oriented, and concatenated, a boundary
     between two pieces supplies a virtual transition which need not be the
     paired transition at the corresponding graph vertex.  Hence the exact
     consequence is that at least one of the four targets must cross a seam,
     not that width-plus-surface length is impossible.  For `m=2`, an
     explicit seven-piece concatenation covers the entire upper half and
     repairs the obstruction in exactly this way.

895. The lexicographic graph has exactly `2m^2+2` vertices of undirected
     degree different from two.  Cutting at them gives

        2m^2+m+4

     maximal forced arms, including the one all-degree-two component cut
     once.  Listing every arm once costs exactly

        |Z_m|+2m^2+m+4

     vertex occurrences before isolated-vertex repairs.  Additional
     surface-many cuts duplicate only cut vertices, never whole long arms.

896. The corrected open upper statement is the Virtual-Seam Excursion
     Lemma: refine the forced arms by `O(m^2)` cuts and choose a signed linear
     order so that every upper target has a facet-spanning below-target run
     inside one piece or across consecutive seams.  Equivalently, the arm
     traces must admit one signed permutation in which every target obtains
     a suffix--whole-blocks--prefix trace chain meeting all four facets.
     This is now an ordering problem on a surface-size kernel, not a local
     pairing problem.  See `LEX_EXCURSION_OBSTRUCTION.md`,
     `LEX_EXCURSION_CONSTRUCTIVE.md`,
     `scratch/check_lex_excursion_obstruction.py`, and
     `scratch/verify_lex_excursion_constructive.py`.

## 223. A width-plus-surface factor for three central layers

897. Let `z in L_(2m)` and let `p<q` be its first two positive coordinates.
     The selected edge joins `z-e_p` to `z-e_q`; define its minimum

        b_z=z-e_p-e_q in L_(2m-2).

     At an endpoint `v`, label the incident half-edge by the coordinate
     omitted from `v` to obtain `b_z`.  Pair two incident half-edges only
     when their labels differ.  Outside

        v_1 in {0,m} or v_2 in {0,m},

     the degree is two and the two labels are `2,1`, so all unpaired
     half-edges and all exceptional transitions have surface order.

898. Decompose the selected edges into transition trails, cut every cycle
     once, and for a trail with edges `e_1,...,e_h` write

        b_(e_1),...,b_(e_h).

     There are only `O(m^2)` pieces.  At an internal transition vertex `v`,
     the different half-edge labels give the exact adjacent factor equation

        b_(e_j) vee b_(e_(j+1)) = v.

     At every nonterminal trail edge of colour `z_j`, the two neighboring
     equations give

        b_(e_(j-1)) vee b_(e_j) vee b_(e_(j+1)) = z_j.

899. Thus the length-`M_m` un-repaired word of edge minima covers all but
     `O(m^2)` values of ranks `2m-1` and `2m`; append those exceptions
     literally.  Its singleton image is exactly

        {x in L_(2m-2): x_1<m and x_2<m}.

     The omitted bottom points have `x_1=m` or `x_2=m`; the two families are
     disjoint and total exactly

        2 C(m,2)=m(m-1).

900. Consequently, for every `m>=2`, there is a nonzero max/OR word of
     length

        M_m+O(m^2)

     covering all three layers `L_(2m-2),L_(2m-1),L_(2m)`.  The deterministic
     checked implementation has the exact length

        M_m+4m^2+4m+2,

     though the robust theorem needs only the surface-order bound.

901. In fixed dimension `t>=3` and any admissible rank `r>m`, the same
     argument covers the three layers `r-2,r-1,r` in

        |L_r^(t)(m)|+O_t(m^(t-2)).

     The proof, two independent audits, and independent multidimensional
     checker are `LEX_THREE_LAYER_FACTOR.md`,
     `LEX_THREE_LAYER_FACTOR_AUDIT.md`,
     `scratch/verify_lex_three_layer_factor.py`, and
     `scratch/audit_lex_three_layer_factor.py`.

902. This is a genuine lower-factor advance and is independent of the false
     within-trail excursion lemma.  At this stage it covered only a constant
     number of layers; Section 224 carries the line factor through every
     sublinear-depth central band.  The remaining lower and upper difficulty
     is linear-depth seam/fan fusion.  Solving that at subcubic total
     overhead would establish the needed four-box constant-one local word.

## 224. Exact line erosion and growing two-sided central bands

903. The regular part of the lexicographic edge-minimum factor is exactly a
     family of coordinate-`{1,2}` lines.  If

        beta_t=(t,K-t,c,d),

     then its `q`-fold sliding intersection is

        gamma_t^(q)=meet_(h=0)^q beta_(t+h)
                   =(t,K-t-q,c,d),

     and every valid consecutive window satisfies the exact factor equation

        join_(h=0)^s gamma_(t+h)^(q)
                   =(t+s,K-t-q,c,d).

     Thus the local erosion iterates to arbitrary depth without an
     approximate distributive-law argument.

904. The singleton image at depth `q` is exactly

        {x in L_(2m-q-2): x_1<=m-q-1, x_2<=m-q-1}.

     Its bottom-layer deficit has the closed form

        D_q=(q+1)m^2-(q+1)^2 m+q(q+1)(q+5)/6.

     Pure equal-rank erosion cannot synthesize any missing bottom target:
     the maximum of equal-rank letters has that same rank only when all
     letters equal the maximum.  This is a scoped boundary obstruction, not
     an obstruction to variable-band completion.

905. Complete the eroded fibres to the full rank

        R=2m-q-2

     coordinate-line word, which has exactly `|L_R|<=M_m` entries.  Append
     the complete three-box slice words `x_1=a` and `x_2=a` for
     `0<=a<=q+1`.  A target of rank `R+s`, `0<=s<=q+2`, is either an
     internal line maximum (`y_1,y_2>=s`) or lies in one of those slices.
     Hence the ranks `R,...,2m` have a word of length

        |L_R|+2(q+2)(m+1)(2m+1)
        <=M_m+O(qm^2).

     In particular every growing depth `q=o(m)` costs only `o(m^3)` beyond
     the four-box width.

906. Shifting the base line gives a two-sided form.  A single rank-`R`
     line spine plus slices `x_1=a,x_2=a` for `0<=a<h` covers every rank
     from `R` through `R+h` in

        |L_R|+2h(m+1)(2m+1)

     positions.  Taking `R=2m-q` and `h=2q` covers
     `L_(2m-q),...,L_(2m+q)`; taking `R=2m-1-q` covers the correspondingly
     shifted symmetric band.  Both have length `M_m+o(m^3)` for `q=o(m)`.

907. The remaining obstruction is now sharply linear-depth.  Independent
     slice fans cost `Theta(qm^2)`, which becomes width-scale for
     `q=Theta(m)`.  A mixed seam between a `{1,2}` line and a `{3,4}` line
     exposes a Cartesian rectangle of suffix--prefix maxima, so a
     surface-size braid has the correct raw portal capacity to fuse those
     slice fans.  Disjoint assignment of those rectangles while retaining
     the factor windows is open.  See `LEX_FACTOR_ITERATION.md`,
     `LEX_FACTOR_ITERATION_AUDIT.md`,
     `LEX_FACTOR_ITERATION_INDEPENDENT_AUDIT.md`, and
     `SHIFTED_LINE_SYMMETRIC_BAND.md` and
     `SHIFTED_LINE_SYMMETRIC_BAND_AUDIT.md`.

## 225. The same lexicographic factor covers four central layers

908. Let `y in L_(2m+1)` and let `i<j` be its first two positive
     coordinates.  The two central colours

        z_i=y-e_i, z_j=y-e_j

     have the common selected-edge endpoint `v=y-e_i-e_j` and satisfy
     `z_i vee z_j=y`.  Except when `y_i=y_j=1`, their half-edge labels at
     `v` are distinct.  In four dimensions the equal-label exception is
     exactly the two targets

        (1,1,m-1,m), (1,1,m,m-1),

     which may be appended literally.

909. If the canonical edges are paired at `v` and neither is a trail-end
     edge, four consecutive edge minima recover `y`: the first three have
     maximum `z_i`, the last three have maximum `z_j`, and the whole
     four-window therefore has maximum `y`.  A distinct-label canonical
     pair can fail to be selected only at a degree-three vertex, of which
     there are `m(m+1)+2`.  Each such vertex is canonical for at most six
     upper targets.

910. If `T=O(m^2)` is the number of transition pieces, at most `2T`
     central edges are first or last in a piece, and each is canonical for
     at most four upper targets.  Hence all new failures number at most

        2+6(m(m+1)+2)+8T=O(m^2).

     Appending them to the audited edge-minimum factor proves that one word
     of length `M_m+O(m^2)` covers all four ranks

        2m-2, 2m-1, 2m, 2m+1.

911. In every fixed dimension `t>=3` the same canonical-pair argument gives
     ranks `r-2,r-1,r,r+1` in

        |L_r^(t)|+O_t(m^(t-2)).

     Equal-label canonical pairs and all non-forced transitions lie in a
     boundary family of the stated order.  The source proof, repaired label
     table, checker, and independent audit are `LEX_FOUR_LAYER_FACTOR.md`,
     `scratch/verify_lex_four_layer_factor.py`, and
     `LEX_FOUR_LAYER_FACTOR_AUDIT.md`.

## 226. Fused slabs, their exact antichain tax, and the portal escape

912. The independent coordinate slices in the growing-band construction can
     be fused into two disjoint thick slabs.  For

        1<=t<=floor((m+1)/2), R=2m-t,
        Psi(d)=ceil(d/2)(floor(d/2)+1),

     an explicit SCD-connector word covers `L_R,...,L_(R+t)` in

        |L_R|+t(2m-t+2)(2m+1)-1-m Psi(t-1)

     positions.  Every witness is a literal interval in the displayed
     descending-chain/ascending-coordinate connector.  Relative to the
     declared uniform `2t(m+1)(2m+1)` slice bound, the exact saving is

        t^2(2m+1)+m Psi(t-1)+1.

     Trimming both old zero-slice origins changes only the final constant by
     two positions.

913. Splitting the first slab into height bands cannot improve this
     connector: the exact identity

        Psi(d)=sum_(j>=0)(d-2j)_+

     gives

        Psi(a+b-1)>=Psi(a-1)+Psi(b-1).

     This optimality statement is scoped to subdivisions using the same
     SCD connector; it is not a lower bound on arbitrary interleavings.

914. A stronger unrestricted lower bound holds whenever the missed central
     targets must be witnessed wholly inside a separate auxiliary word.
     The boundary family

        B_(m,t)={y in L_(2m): y_1<t or y_2<t}

     is an antichain of exact size

        t m^2+t(t+2)m+t(5+3t-5t^2)/3.

     A word of length `v` contains at most `v` pairwise nonnesting selected
     intervals, so any separated auxiliary word covering this family has at
     least `|B_(m,t)|` positions.

915. Since

        M_m-|L_(2m-t)|=t^2m+t-t(t-1)^2/2,

     every such separated construction has total length at least

        M_m+t m(m+2)-7t(t^2-1)/6.

     For `t=o(m)` the excess is `(1-o(1))tm^2`; for
     `t=alpha m`, `0<alpha<=1/2`, it is

        (alpha-7alpha^3/6)m^3+O(m^2)>0.

     This rules out every internally witnessed slab hierarchy, regardless
     of how its logical subslabs share physical descriptions.  It does not
     apply to witnesses crossing the main spine.

916. The exact escape is a complementary-line corner portal.  If two
     consecutive line pieces through a base point `v` transfer independently
     in disjoint coordinate pairs, then the interval using `u` letters on
     the first side and `w` on the second has maximum

        v+u e_(i')+w e_j.

     One seam therefore supplies a Cartesian rectangle of targets and all
     smaller depths simultaneously.  A bounded-overlap portal braid with
     `O(m^2)` seams and only `o(m^3)` repeated base points would give the
     desired linear-depth word.  Its existence remains open.  See
     `MULTISCALE_SLAB_FUSION.md` and
     `MULTISCALE_SLAB_FUSION_AUDIT.md`.

## 227. Bounded-depth virtual seams and lossless arm-to-factor coupling

917. For an upper target `y` of rank `2m+D`, every vertex on its canonical
     reverse-greedy path has deficit vector `delta=y-v` of mass `D+1`.
     The lexicographic potential `sum_i i v_i` therefore ranges across an
     interval of width at most `3(D+1)`, so the directed path has at most
     `3(D+1)` edges.  If it avoids the cut kernel of at most `2m^2+3`
     vertices, it lies in one forced arm and is already contiguous.

918. For depth at most `q`, a fixed kernel vertex is below at most
     `C(q+5,4)` target deficit vectors.  Appending one canonical path for
     each exceptional target gives an explicit rank-`(2m-1)` word of length

        M_m+O(m^2(q+1)^5)

     covering all ranks from `2m-1` through `2m+q`.  Thus every fixed depth
     has surface error, and `q=o(m^(1/5))` has subcubic error.  If arbitrary
     nonzero repair letters are allowed, appending the exceptional targets
     themselves improves this to `O(m^2(q+1)^4)` and
     `q=o(m^(1/4))`.  These are weaker in depth than the shifted-line band,
     but they preserve the lexicographic arm architecture needed for an
     all-upper ordering.

919. Quadratically many virtual seams are necessary in any edge-once signed
     arm ordering.  The hard rank-`(2m+1)` family

        (0,a,b,c) and (a,0,b,c),
        2<=a,b,c<=m-1, a+b+c=2m+1,

     has `(m-2)(m-3)` members, none witnessed inside one forced arm.  A
     selected witness meets at most five blocks, and for a fixed leftmost
     seam and terminal block the two endpoint-max chains give at most nine
     rank-`(2m+1)` values.  Hence one seam receives at most `36` charges and
     at least

        (m-2)(m-3)/36

     active seams are required.  This matches, rather than exceeds, the
     available `Theta(m^2)` seam budget.

920. There is a lossless coupling from a vertex-arm word to the lower
     edge-minimum factor.  Encode

        v_0,e_1,v_1,...,e_h,v_h

     by

        v_0,b_(e_1),...,b_(e_h),v_h.

     Every original vertex-subpath maximum is represented by the interval
     starting at `v_0` or `b_(e_i)` and ending at `v_h` or
     `b_(e_(j+1))`.  The maximum is exact because internal vertices are
     adjacent joins of their two edge minima.  This mapping also preserves
     intervals crossing arbitrary virtual seams.

921. The degree-defined forced arms require one refinement before this
     lift.  Exactly `2(m-1)` internal degree-two vertices have equal
     half-edge labels:

        (0,m,a,m-1-a), (m,0,a,m-1-a), 1<=a<=m-1.

     Cut there and keep each pair of child pieces consecutive in its old
     orientation.  The duplicated literal vertex preserves every upper
     interval, and all remaining internal transitions satisfy the lower
     factor equation.  The encoded word has one minimum per central edge
     plus two endpoints per surface-many piece, hence length
     `M_m+O(m^2)`.

922. Consequently, any future seam-aware forced-arm ordering covering the
     upper half automatically lifts to the same asymptotic word covering
     the upper family and the three layers `2m-2,2m-1,2m`; there is no
     separate global pinning problem for this spine.  The all-upper signed
     ordering remains open.  See `VIRTUAL_SEAM_TRACE_STITCHING.md`, its
     independent audit, `ARM_WORD_FACTOR_LIFT.md`, and
     `ARM_WORD_FACTOR_LIFT_AUDIT.md`.

## 228. A near-once linear-depth portal core

923. Put `R=2m-1` and let `1<=q<=floor(m/3)`.  There is an explicit word
     on rank-`R` points which contains every point of `L_R` at least once
     and at most twice, has the exact length

        |L_R|+4q(q-1)=M_m+O(m^2),

     and covers, for every `1<=s<=q`, every target `y in L_(R+s)` missed by
     both complementary complete-line systems:

        min(y_1,y_2)<s and min(y_3,y_4)<s.

     Thus a genuine positive linear-depth family already fits in a
     near-once central word; raw portal capacity is not the obstruction.

924. Every such target has a unique high/low orientation.  In one
     orientation write

        y=(m-A,a,m-B,b),
        0<=a,b<=s-1,
        A+B=a+b-s+1=delta.

     Then `0<=delta<=s-1` and `A,B<=a,b`.  For every
     `A+B<=q-1`, use the physical complementary arms

        X_u=(m-A-u,B+u,m-B-1,A),
        Y_v=(m-A-1,B,m-B-v,A+v),

     with the `X` arm reversed into the `Y` arm.  The suffix--prefix
     interval has maximum

        (m-A,B+u,m-B,A+v).

     Choosing `u=a-B`, `v=b-A` represents `y` in exactly `s+1` letters.

925. Within one orientation all `X` letters are distinct and all `Y`
     letters are distinct.  A cross-type collision occurs only when the
     two arm parameters sum to one.  There are exactly `q(q-1)` repeated
     points per orientation.  The four orientations are disjoint because
     every designated high coordinate is at least `m-2q+2>q-1`, while its
     paired low coordinate is at most `q-1`.  Appending every unused base
     point once gives the exact length in item 923.

926. The hard family at exact depth `s` has size `4 C(s+2,3)`, hence the
     portal core covers `4 C(q+3,4)=Theta(q^4)` genuinely mixed targets
     through depth `q`, with only `4q(q-1)` repeated occurrences.  Every
     internal arm interval retains the exact line sliding-rank equation.

927. This does not yet cover the whole band.  Targets easy for one complete
     line direction may lose their witnesses when the portal arms are cut
     out and moved.  A min-comparison partition reduces the remaining tie
     strip to a balanced line-demand catalogue.  For the canonical baseline

        (floor(delta/2),ceil(delta/2)),

     each physical line is requested at most twice, so the bipartite demand
     graph is a union of paths and cycles.  Arbitrarily reversing odd
     baselines can raise the degree to three, and boundary odd requests need
     not collide with even requests; neither stronger simplification may be
     assumed.

928. The exact remaining upper-band lemma is therefore a bounded-degree
     line-demand braid: choose baselines, cuts, orientations, and segment
     order so the portal rectangles cover the tie strip, preferred easy
     line intervals remain contiguous, and only `o(m^3)` base occurrences
     repeat.  The main portal theorem, collision count, and parameter range
     have passed independent audit.  See
     `COMPLEMENTARY_SEAM_RECTANGLE_TILING.md`,
     `COMPLEMENTARY_SEAM_RECTANGLE_TILING_AUDIT.md`, and
     `scratch/verify_complementary_seam_rectangles.py`.

## 229. Two scoped physical-order barriers for literal portal completion

929. The first literal completion of the hard portal core is impossible at
     near-once linear depth.  Let the portal-touched coordinate-{1,2} and
     coordinate-{3,4} line families be completed strongly enough that every
     adjacent lattice pair on every such line remains adjacent somewhere in
     the word.  If

        n_q(d)=floor((q+1-|d|)/2) for |d|<=q-1

     and zero otherwise, put

        S_q=sum_d n_q(d)n_q(d-1),   J_q=4S_(q-1).

     The exact formulas are

        J_q = q(2q+1)(q-2)/3                 (q even),
        J_q = [q(2q+1)(q-2)+3]/3             (q odd).

     There are exactly J_q physical points interior in one line of each
     complementary family.  Each needs four distinct word adjacencies, so
     it must occur at least twice.  Therefore every such
     adjacency-preserving completion has

        |W|-|L_(2m-1)| >= J_q = (2/3)q^3+O(q^2).

     The count and word argument passed independent audit.  This does not
     exclude a target-selective completion which discards one local line
     direction at a crossing.  See PORTAL_EASY_LINE_COMPLETION.md,
     PORTAL_EASY_LINE_COMPLETION_AUDIT.md, and
     scratch/verify_portal_easy_line_completion.py.

930. The balanced tie-strip demand graph is now explicit.  In one fixed
     high/low orientation, an even seam A+B=2r is the edge

        X_(B,r) -- Y_(A,r).

     An odd seam A+B=2r+1 is either

        X_(B,r+1) -- Y_(A,r)    (canonical),
        X_(B,r)   -- Y_(A,r+1)  (reversed).

     With all canonical choices, every component is one finite diagonal
     path, with invariant kappa=A-B on even seams and kappa=A-B+1 on odd
     seams.  There are only O(m) such paths.  Under arbitrary
     degree-controlled odd choices, contraction of the even seams gives a
     subgraph of a doubled path.  Hence every component is a path or an
     elementary alternating four-cycle; no longer cycle exists.  Every
     four-cycle contains one canonical and one reversed odd bridge, so its
     balanced-sheet xor monodromy is one and one cut removes it.

931. That incidence simplification does not solve the physical braid.  On
     a preferred physical line write the boundary ray as

        p_0,p_1,p_2,...

     An even balanced seam uses p_0 at both line ends.  Every odd balanced
     seam, under either baseline choice, uses p_(-1) on one line and p_1 on
     the complementary line.  Reversing the baseline only swaps which
     direction has the inward p_1 defect.

     Retaining the literal easy depth-q block

        p_0,p_1,...,p_q

     while also using the literal inward portal arm

        p_1,p_2,...,p_(q-1)

     forces a second occurrence of every point of the latter arm: in the
     easy block, the outward neighbor of p_1 is p_0, whereas in the portal
     block it must be the opposite seam corner.

932. Put t=floor((m-q-1)/3).  In one fixed orientation the interior labels

        A+B=2r+1, 1<=r<=t, A>=1, B>=1,

     give t(t+1) demanded odd seams with legal full depth-q arms.  The two
     extreme labels at each level must be omitted: for one baseline choice
     their formal p_0 lies outside the box, so the preferred segment begins
     at p_1 and the easy and portal occurrences need not be distinct.  The
     retained interior labels avoid this boundary escape.  Their
     inward physical lines are injective within each line direction, and a
     base point lies on at most one forced line of each direction.
     Consequently every word preserving those literal easy blocks and
     balanced portal arms has at least

        [t(t+1)(q-1)]/2 = Omega(qm^2)

     repeated occurrences.  A direct constant-copy construction--keep the
     preferred line blocks and append every balanced portal block--has
     O(qm^2) repeats, so this order is sharp for the literal architecture.
     At q=Theta(m) the cost is Theta(m^3), and the proposed O(m^2)-repeat
     balanced braid is false.

     This is a scoped architectural no-go, not a general upper-band
     impossibility.  A successful near-once construction must let mixed
     seams replace the easy witnesses near inward cuts, or otherwise abandon
     the simultaneous literal-arm/intact-line requirements.  See
     BALANCED_LINE_DEMAND_BRAID.md and
     BALANCED_LINE_DEMAND_BRAID_AUDIT.md.

## 230. Rounded portal factors and the macroscopic-reservoir theorem

933. A nondegenerate complementary portal corner admits a one-point
     factor-compatible rounding.  If the two rank-`R=2m-1` corners are

        X_0=Z-e_(h_2),  Y_0=Z-e_(h_1),  |Z|=2m,

     and a low coordinate `j` of `Z` is positive, insert

        W=Z-e_j

     between them.  Every old interval crossing the corner already has
     maximum at least `Z`, while `W<=Z`, so every old maximum is unchanged.
     At the three internal positions the adjacent edge-minimum labels are,
     when the inherited line neighbours exist,

        (h_1,j), (h_2,h_1), (j,h_2),

     and are distinct in each pair.  Missing inherited neighbours make the
     corresponding corner a literal component endpoint.  The unique seam
     with no positive low coordinate is cut instead.

934. Applying `ARM_WORD_FACTOR_LIFT` after these roundings preserves every
     upper portal interval and gives an occurrence-by-occurrence first
     factor at surface cost.  The hard swapped-baseline catalogue requires
     `O(q^2)` rounded occurrences; the full balanced catalogue requires at
     most `O(m^2)`.  Coverage of the complete next lower layer is not
     automatic.  A sufficient and genuinely additional condition is that
     every `x in L_(R-1)` have two distinct legal upper covers
     `x+e_i,x+e_j` retained as an adjacency.  Surface-many cut retained
     edges can be repaired literally, but this does not repair a large
     family of lower covers never selected by the upper braid.

935. The maximal factor is not self-similar at a rounded corner.  Locally
     its four first minima are

        b_0=b_3=Z-e_1-e_3,
        b_1=Z-e_2-e_3,
        b_2=Z-e_1-e_2,

     after relabelling.  All three adjacent second minima equal
     `Z-e_1-e_2-e_3`, so the maximal second factor cannot recover `b_1` or
     `b_2`.  This disproves naive maximal iteration only; a sparse
     self-similar pin factor remains open.

936. There is a general endpoint-supply obstruction for a prescribed linked
     occurrence band.  Let a rank-`R` occurrence row `T_1,...,T_L` be
     represented in a word of length `L+d` on intervals

        I_i=[i+alpha_i,i+beta_i]

     with both offset sequences nondecreasing.  Suppose a coordinate
     threshold atom forms an internal singleton at least once every `H`
     row positions, including the two boundary gaps.  Then the exact
     singleton-run inequality and telescoping give

        sum_i (beta_i-alpha_i) <= 3Hd+2d.

     If the same word covers every nonzero point below rank `R=2m-1`, then

        d >= (m^4+2m^3-m-2) / [2(3H+2m)].

     The proof groups arbitrary lower witnesses by right endpoint.  At a
     selected central endpoint only `beta_i-alpha_i` lower starts are
     possible; the `d` unselected endpoints carry chains of at most
     `2m-2` lower targets.  Thus `H=O(m)` forces `d=Omega(m^3)`.

937. The theorem in Item 936 is conditional on the displayed
     occurrence-by-occurrence linked band.  The equal-rank normal form gives
     such a band for one witness per distinct target, but does not
     automatically order every repeated occurrence of an arbitrary portal
     word.  It is therefore not an unrestricted lower bound for every
     equality or near-width word.

938. A bounded-run extension is also proved.  For ordered, position-disjoint
     maximal atom runs of length at most `C`, separated by gaps at most `H`,

        sum_i w_i <= (3H+2C)d+(C-1)(H+C)s.

     The corresponding endpoint inequality is

        d >= [ (m^4+2m^3-m-2)/2 -(C-1)(H+C)s ]
             / [3H+2C+2m-2].

     Rounded corners give `C=2`.  Hence a linked rounded braid with
     `s=O(m^2)` position-disjoint turns and `H=O(m)` still needs cubic
     slack.  A near-width lower factor must cluster its sharp turns and
     leave a seam-free reservoir of length `Omega(m^2)`, replace most turns
     by nonsharp shared-pin transitions, or abandon this linked band.

939. The source proofs and two independent audits are
     `PORTAL_LINEAR_FACTOR_COUPLING.md`,
     `PORTAL_LINEAR_FACTOR_COUPLING_AUDIT.md`, and
     `PORTAL_LINEAR_FACTOR_COUPLING_INDEPENDENT_AUDIT.md`.  The finite
     checkers verify 9,425 rounded corners, 2,573,727 singleton schedules,
     and 66,210 bounded-run schedules.  All conclusions above retain the
     scope in Item 937.

## 231. Null audit of the rank-strip LP

940. The reported odd-dimensional LP equalities `minholes=allowed` are
     forced by the LP's own equality constraints.  Summing the three
     physical-row equations and subtracting the rank-total equations fixes

        h_0+h_1+h_2
          =3M+6-sum_(s=1)^r C(k,s),

     which is exactly both the minimized objective and the printed residual
     `sigma`.  The experiment therefore proves only feasibility of its
     coarse rank-marginal relaxation; it supplies neither evidence for the
     exact conjecture nor the announced but unstated two-core theorem.  See
     `RANK_STRIP_LP_NULL_AUDIT.md`.

## 232. Quantitative audit of the radius-typed matching route

941. No currently available nibble or pseudorandom matching theorem closes
     the typed fractional rounding target in Sections 8--12 of
     `PARTIAL_BLOCK_MULTISCALE.md`.  Through

        H=sqrt(m) omega(1),

     the certified band has

        V_H=(sqrt(pi)+o(1)) W sqrt(m)

     vertices.  The typed edge has maximum and average sizes

        K_max=(4+o(1)) ell H,
        K_av=(2sqrt(pi)+o(1)) ell sqrt(m).

     The exact worst weighted pair load is already bounded below and above
     by

        2/(m+1) <= delta_2^(x) <= 2/(m-H).

942. In Gould--Kelly's quantitative nibble, the available pseudorandomness
     parameter therefore satisfies at best

        B <= sqrt((m+1)/2).

     Even before its actual polylogarithmic loss, the nominal leftover is at
     least

        V_H/B=(sqrt(2pi)+o(1))W,

     rather than `o(W)`.  The exact loss in the primary source is
     `B^(-1+gamma)(log D)^A`.  Its allowed weight support is
     `D^(log D)`, so the `2H+1` rank indicators fit; weight complexity is not
     the obstruction.  Ehard--Glock--Joos has error
     `m^(-1/(50K^2))=1-o(1)` here, and the genuinely growing-uniformity
     Alon--Bollobas--Kim--Vu theorem also fails its explicit parameter
     condition by a large margin.

943. The exact missing black box would have to exploit chain-bundle
     geometry and leave

        o(V_H/sqrt(m))=o(W)

     vertices.  Degree and pair-codegree information alone cannot imply
     this, as projective planes have comparable normalized codegrees and
     matching number one.  Thus quoting a stronger general nibble is not a
     valid completion.  The source-level audit is
     `TYPED_MATCHING_QUANTITATIVE_AUDIT.md`.

## 233. Algebraic rigidity of shift-compatible SCD projections

944. Let `F(x)=Ax+b` be an affine permutation of an orientation cube
     `F_2^s`, and put `r=rank(A+I)`.  The exact fraction of vertices on which
     `F` is a Hamming-neighbour map is at most

        (r+1)/2^r.

     Consequently, if this fraction is `1-o(1)`, it is eventually one.
     Every full-neighbour affine permutation then has order at most four.
     Since the shift recurrence forces the cycle containing a radius-`d`
     centre to have length strictly greater than `d`, one affine successor
     per orientation stratum cannot support the unbounded radii required by
     a near wreath-resolved SCD.

945. There is also an exact obstruction to a fixed ground-coordinate
     action.  If a coordinate permutation `g` has cycle lengths `ell_i` and
     `c` cycles, the number of subsets `X` satisfying both

        |X triangle gX|=2

     and `g`-orbit length at least `L` is exactly

        2^(c-1) sum_(ell_i>=L) ell_i(ell_i-1)

     and is at most `n^2 2^(n-L)`.  A positive fraction of SCD centres have
     radius in `[sqrt(m),2sqrt(m)]`; hence any construction whose bundles
     are literal orbits of fixed coordinate permutations needs at least

        Omega(2^(sqrt(m))/m^(5/2))

     distinct generators.  Bounded, polynomial, and
     `exp(o(sqrt(m)))` template libraries are excluded.

946. These results do not exclude state-dependent nonlinear successors,
     exponentially many unrelated wreath orders, or a genuine
     Baranyai-style resolution.  The proofs, adversarial audit, and
     exhaustive checker are `SHIFT_COMPATIBLE_SCD_ALGEBRA.md`,
     `SHIFT_COMPATIBLE_SCD_ALGEBRA_AUDIT.md`, and
     `scratch/verify_shift_scd_algebra.cpp`; the checker exhausts affine
     maps through dimension four and coordinate permutations through eight
     points.

## 234. Exact multistage shadow-extension ledger

947. For one fixed depth `q`, let `Q_q` have lower and upper shadow classes
     at ranks `m-q,m+q` and `q+1` positional clones of the middle layer.
     A directed geodesic Johnson `q`-path is one hyperedge.  Its exact
     degrees are

        D_T=(m)_q(m+1)_q,
        D_M=(m)_q^2,
        D_T/D_M=1/rho_q.

     The exact nonzero pair-codegree ratios are

        (2q)!/(m)_q^2,  1/C(m,q),  1/C(m,d)^2.

     Hence the normalized maximum pair codegree is `1/m` at `q=1` and
     `O(1/m^2)` uniformly for `2<=q=o(m)`.  Every fixed marginal depth is
     therefore nibble-easy.

948. Marginal matchings do not assemble automatically.  The prefix/suffix
     history space for a `q`-window has size

        W(m)_(q-1)^2.

     Unrelated near-perfect matchings have essentially no shift overlap in
     that space.  Cloning targets corrects degree imbalance but does not
     create the positive de-Bruijn recurrence needed for one word.

949. Let a depth-one two-sided-rainbow linear forest have

        |E|=N_1-e,
        c=Cat_m+e

     components.  Its number of internal `q`-paths is

        P_q=sum_i(v_i-q)_+ >= N_q-qe,

     using the exact inequality `rho_q<=1-q/(m+1)`.  Thus the unavoidable
     Catalan component count is already paid for by binomial rank shrinkage;
     only the excess `e` costs up to `qe` windows at depth `q`, or
     `eH(H+1)/2` cumulatively.

950. For an `H`-geodesic forest, let `E_q` be its correct-rank depth-`q`
     windows, `M_q` the number of missing targets on one side, and `D_q` the
     linear duplicate excess.  The exact identity is

        M_q=D_q-(E_q-N_q).

     This distinguishes actual repair cost from collision counts.  At each
     depth form the bipartite shadow multigraph `Gamma_q` between lower and
     upper targets.  If its matching deficiency is `kappa_q`, then both
     one-sided missing counts are at most `kappa_q`; the matchings at
     different depths need not be nested.

951. The following row-level statement is sufficient for asymptotic
     optimality.  For

        H/sqrt(m)->infinity,  H=o(m^(2/3)),

     construct an `H`-geodesic spanning middle-layer forest with component
     count `c` and actual shadow omissions satisfying

        Hc=o(W),
        sum_(q<=H)(M_q^-+M_q^+)=o(W).

     Blockwise maximal erosion costs exactly `W+Hc`; the missing band masks
     and the truncated outer ideals cost `o(W)`.  Therefore this statement
     implies `nu(2m)=W+o(W)`.  The stronger checkable condition

        sum_(q<=H) kappa_q=o(W)

     also suffices.  This target is weaker than a nested or wreath-resolved
     SCD but still contains the essential positive shift structure.

952. Local switching cannot manufacture that structure after the fact:
     changing `s` transitions changes at most `qs` depth-`q` windows and at
     most `sH(H+1)` windows cumulatively.  Shallow absorber roots number only
     `O(q^2W/m)` in the ideal component regime.  The current depth-one
     theorem must therefore be rebuilt with shift overlap from the outset,
     not post-processed independently by depth.  The complete proof and
     boundary audit are `MULTISTAGE_SHADOW_EXTENSION.md` and
     `MULTISTAGE_SHADOW_EXTENSION_AUDIT.md`.

## 235. Radius-pure isometric Bender--Knuth host cubes

953. Binary RSK identifies a two-row standard tableau with a ballot word.
     Match its `U,D` steps by the usual stack rule.  The balanced binary
     middle word puts opposite bits on every matched pair and splits the
     `2d` persistent `U` steps into `d` zeros followed by `d` ones, where
     `d` is the RSK radius.  Group labels into the odd pairs

        (1,2),(3,4),...,(2m-1,2m).

     The commuting odd Bender--Knuth generator is active exactly on a mixed
     `UD` or `DU` block above height zero.

954. There is an exact carrier formula for the actual Johnson support of
     every such generator.  Outside certain final persistent low-level
     sequences its support is the native ground-coordinate pair

        {2j-1,2j}.

     Inside one critical sequence, the support is determined by the most
     recent carrier update and by whether a later `DU` update occurs.  This
     yields an exact twist graph on the active odd generators: two
     generators are adjacent precisely when their commuting square changes
     the opposite physical supports.

955. If `C` is any vertex cover of this twist graph and `K` its complement,
     then the complete `K`-orbit through the tableau is a genuine isometric
     coordinate-pair cube in `J(2m,m)`.  Every retained direction has one
     fixed two-coordinate support throughout the subcube, the supports are
     pairwise disjoint, and the entire cube stays in the same RSK radius
     class.

956. A proposed `exp((log 3+o(1))m)` bound on total twist incidence is
     false.  The block family

        UU, UD, UD, E, UU,
